title.zh: 卷四百二十六 列傳第一百八十五 循吏 陳靖 張綸 邵曄 崔立 魯有開 張逸 吳遵路 趙尚寬 高賦 程師孟 韓晉卿 葉康直
title.en: Volume 426 Biographies 185: Xun Li, Chen Jing, Zhang Lun, Shao Ye, Cui Li, Lu Youkai, Zhang Yi, Wu Zunlu, Zhao Shangkuan, Gao Fu, Cheng Shimeng, Han Jinqing, Ye Kangzhi
title.raw: 卷四百二十六 列傳第一百八十五 循吏 陳靖 張綸 邵曄 崔立 魯有開 張逸 吳遵路 趙尚寬 高賦 程師孟 韓晉卿 葉康直 Volume 426 Biographies 185: Xun Li, Chen Jing, Zhang Lun, Shao Ye, Cui Li, Lu Youkai, Zhang Yi, Wu Zunlu, Zhao Shangkuan, Gao Fu, Cheng Shimeng, Han Jinqing, Ye Kangzhi

sentences.zh: 〇陳靖張綸邵曄崔立魯有開張逸吳遵路趙尚寬高賦程師孟韓晉卿葉康直

translations.literal: Chen Jing, Zhang Lun, Shao Ye, Cui Li, Lu Youkai, Zhang Yi, Wu Zunlu, Zhao Shangkuan, Gao Fu, Cheng Shimeng, Han Jinqing, Ye Kangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing, Zhang Lun, Shao Ye, Cui Li, Lu Youkai, Zhang Yi, Wu Zunlu, Zhao Shangkuan, Gao Fu, Cheng Shimeng, Han Jinqing, and Ye Kangzhi.

sentences.zh: 宋法有可以得循吏者三：太祖之世，牧守令錄，躬自召見，問以政事，然後遣行，簡擇之道精矣；

translations.literal: Song law had three means by which virtuous officials could be obtained: in the era of Taizu, governors, prefects, and magistrates were registered; he personally summoned them for audience, questioned them on governance affairs, and only then dispatched them—the way of selection was refined;
translations.idiomatic: Song law offered three ways to produce virtuous officials: under Taizu, governors, prefects, and magistrates were registered, summoned in person, questioned on how they would govern, and only then sent out—selection had become exacting;

sentences.zh: 監司察郡守，郡守察縣令，各以時上其殿最，又命朝臣專督治之，考課之方密矣；

translations.literal: circuit commissioners inspected prefects, prefects inspected county magistrates, each in season reported their grades of merit and demerit, and moreover court officials were appointed specifically to supervise their governance—the methods of evaluation were thorough;
translations.idiomatic: circuit commissioners watched prefects, prefects watched county magistrates, and each reported merit rankings on schedule; court officials were also assigned to oversee governance directly—evaluation had grown rigorous;

sentences.zh: 吏犯贓遇赦不原，防閑之令嚴矣。

translations.literal: officials guilty of corruption were not pardoned on general amnesty—the preventive regulations were strict.
translations.idiomatic: officials who took bribes were never restored by amnesty—safeguards against abuse were stern.

sentences.zh: 承平之世，州縣吏謹守法度以修其職業者，實多其人。

translations.literal: In the era of peace and prosperity, there were indeed many prefectural and county officials who diligently observed the laws in performing their duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the long peace, many prefectural and county officers dutifully kept the law and did their jobs well.

sentences.zh: 其間必有絕異之績，然後別於賞令，或自州縣善最，他日遂為名臣，則撫子之長又不足以盡其平生，故始終三百餘年，循吏載諸簡策者十二人。

translations.literal: Among them there had to be exceptionally outstanding achievements before they were distinguished in reward edicts, or starting from excellent records at prefecture and county they later became renowned ministers—then the length of a gazetteer biography would not suffice to encompass their whole lives; thus over more than three hundred years from beginning to end, twelve virtuous officials are recorded in the historical documents.
translations.idiomatic: Only those with truly extraordinary service were singled out in reward edicts; some rose from excellent county or prefectural records to become famous ministers at court, and a standard biography could not hold their whole careers. Across more than three hundred years, only twelve virtuous officials earned a place in the annals.

sentences.zh: 作《循吏傳》。

translations.literal: [I] composed the "Biographies of Virtuous Officials."
translations.idiomatic: Hence this "Biographies of Virtuous Officials."

sentences.zh: 陳靖，字道卿，興化軍莆田人。

translations.literal: Chen Jing, styled Daqing, was a native of Putian in the Xinghua Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing, courtesy name Daqing, came from Putian in the Xinghua Commandery.

sentences.zh: 好學，頗通古今。

translations.literal: He was fond of learning and was quite versed in affairs past and present.
translations.idiomatic: He loved study and knew the past and present well.

sentences.zh: 父仁壁，仕陳洪進為泉州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Renbi served Chen Hongjin as Vice Magistrate of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Renbi had served Chen Hongjin as vice magistrate of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪進稱臣，豪猾有負險為亂者，靖徒步謁轉運使楊克巽，陳討賊策。

translations.literal: When Hongjin submitted to the throne, powerful ruffians took advantage of difficult terrain to cause turmoil; Jing went on foot to visit Transport Commissioner Yang Kexun and presented a plan to suppress the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongjin submitted to the Song, local strongmen used the hills to raise trouble; Jing walked to Transport Commissioner Yang Kexun and laid out a plan to crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 召還，授陽翟縣主簿。

translations.literal: He was summoned back and appointed Registrar of Yangzhai County.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made registrar of Yangzhai County.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯邊，王師數不利，靖遣從子上書，求入奏機略。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the frontier and imperial forces suffered repeated defeats, Jing sent his son by a concubine to submit a memorial requesting permission to come to court and report strategic plans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided the border and imperial armies kept losing, Jing sent a son by a concubine to memorialize the throne, asking leave to present strategy in person.

sentences.zh: 詔就問之，上五策，曰：明賞罰；

translations.literal: An edict summoned him for questioning; he submitted five stratagems, saying: clarify rewards and punishments;
translations.idiomatic: The court called him in and he offered five measures: make rewards and punishments clear;

sentences.zh: 撫士眾；

translations.literal: comfort the troops;
translations.idiomatic: steady the soldiers;

sentences.zh: 持重示弱，待利而舉；

translations.literal: hold firm and show weakness, wait for advantage before acting;
translations.idiomatic: stand firm, feign weakness, and strike only when the moment favors you;

sentences.zh: 帥府許自辟士；

translations.literal: allow military headquarters to recruit men on their own authority;
translations.idiomatic: let commanders recruit their own staff;

sentences.zh: 而將帥得專制境外。

translations.literal: and let generals exercise independent control beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: and give generals full discretion beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 太宗異之，改將作監丞，未幾，為御史臺推勘官。

translations.literal: Taizong was impressed and changed [his appointment] to Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings; before long he became Investigating Officer of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong took notice and moved him to the Directorate for Palace Buildings; soon after he became an investigating officer of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 時禦試進士，多擢文先就者為高等，士皆習浮華，尚敏速。

translations.literal: At that time in the imperial examination for advanced scholars, many who finished their essays first were placed in high grades; scholars all cultivated flashy style and valued speed.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace examination for jinshi, candidates who finished their essays first were often ranked highest, so students prized flash and speed over depth.

sentences.zh: 靖請以文付考官第甲乙，俟唱名，或果知名士，即置上科。

translations.literal: Jing requested that essays be given to examiners for grading into first and second ranks, and only when names were called out—if someone proved to be a renowned scholar—should he be placed in the top rank.
translations.idiomatic: Jing proposed that examiners grade the papers as first or second class in advance, and only at the public roll call move a truly famous scholar into the top tier.

sentences.zh: 喪父，起復秘書丞，直史館，判三司開拆司。

translations.literal: On his father's death he left mourning and was appointed Secretariat Director, Hanlin Academician, and judged the Three Departments Document Unsealing Office.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he left mourning early, became a secretariat director and Hanlin academician, and oversaw the Three Departments document unsealing office.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，使高麗還，提點在京百司，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, after an embassy to Goryeo he returned and was made Intendant of the Hundred Offices in the capital, then promoted to Erudite of the Directorate of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 4, returning from an embassy to Goryeo, he was made intendant of capital offices and then promoted to erudite of the Directorate of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 太宗務興農事，詔有司議均田法，靖議曰：「法未易遽行也。

translations.literal: Taizong devoted himself to promoting agriculture and ordered relevant offices to discuss the equal-field law. Jing argued: "The law cannot be hurried into implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong pressed to revive farming and ordered officials to debate the equal-field system. Jing argued, "That law cannot be rushed into force.

sentences.zh: 宜先命大臣或三司使為租庸使，或兼屯田制置，仍擇三司判官選通知民事者二人為之貳。

translations.literal: First one should order a great minister or the Commissioner of the Three Departments to serve as Zu Yong commissioner, or concurrently as Commissioner for Frontier Colonies and Field Systems, and additionally select two Three Departments judges versed in civilian affairs to serve as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: First appoint a senior minister or the Three Departments commissioner as rent-and-corvée commissioner, or add the title of frontier colony commissioner, and choose two Three Departments judges who understand rural affairs as deputies.

sentences.zh: 兩京東西千里，檢責荒地及逃民產籍之，募耕作，賜耕者室廬、牛犁、種食，不足則給以庫錢。

translations.literal: Within a thousand li east and west of the two capitals, investigate and register wasteland and the property registers of fugitive populations; recruit them to cultivate, and grant cultivators houses, oxen, plows, and seed—if insufficient, supply from treasury funds.
translations.idiomatic: For a thousand li east and west of the two capitals, survey wasteland and the property rolls of fugitives, recruit them to farm, and grant houses, oxen, plows, and seed; where that falls short, pay from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 別其課為十分，責州縣勸課，給印紙書之。

translations.literal: Separate their tax obligations into ten parts, charge prefectures and counties to urge farming, and issue sealed documents recording it.
translations.idiomatic: Divide their tax quota into tenths, hold prefectures and counties responsible for urging cultivation, and issue stamped documents to record it.

sentences.zh: 分殿最為三等：凡縣管墾田，一歲得課三分，二歲六分，三歲九分，為下最；

translations.literal: Divide grades of merit into three classes: for any county managing reclaimed fields, one year achieving three-tenths of the tax quota, two years six-tenths, three years nine-tenths—lowest grade;
translations.idiomatic: Merit grades fell into three tiers: a county that brought wasteland under cultivation and met three-tenths of the quota in one year, six in two, nine in three, ranked lowest;

sentences.zh: 一歲四分，二歲七分，三歲至十分，為中最；

translations.literal: one year four-tenths, two years seven-tenths, three years up to full ten-tenths—middle grade;
translations.idiomatic: four-tenths in one year, seven in two, full quota in three, ranked middle;

sentences.zh: 一歲五分，未及三歲盈十分者，為上最。

translations.literal: one year five-tenths, and before three years exceeding full ten-tenths—highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: five-tenths in one year, or exceeding the full quota before three years, ranked highest.

sentences.zh: 其最者，令佐免選或超資；

translations.literal: For the highest, magistrates and assistants were exempted from selection or granted extraordinary promotion;
translations.idiomatic: Top performers won exemption from the regular promotion cycle or fast-track advancement;

sentences.zh: 殿者，即增選降資。

translations.literal: for the lowest, their selection was increased [in wait time] and their rank reduced.
translations.idiomatic: bottom ranks faced longer waits for promotion and demotion in rank.

sentences.zh: 每州通以諸縣田為十分，視殿最行賞罰。

translations.literal: Each prefecture totaled all county fields as ten parts and applied rewards and punishments according to grades.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture pooled its counties' fields as ten shares and rewarded or punished by the combined grade.

sentences.zh: 候數歲，盡罷官屯田，悉用賦民，然後量人授田，度地均稅，約井田之制，為定以法，頒行四方，不過如此矣。」

translations.literal: After several years, entirely abolish official colony fields, fully apply tax to the people, then measure people to grant fields, measure land to equalize tax, approximate the well-field system as fixed law, promulgate to the four quarters—not beyond this."
translations.idiomatic: After a few years, abolish government colony farms, tax the people directly, then allot fields by household and equalize tax by land, approximating the well-field model as permanent law for the empire—nothing more was needed."

sentences.zh: 太宗謂呂端曰：「朕欲復井田，顧未能也，靖此策合朕意。」

translations.literal: Taizong said to Lü Duan: "I wish to restore the well-field system but have not yet been able; Jing's plan fits my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told Lü Duan, "I want to restore the well-field system but have not managed it; Jing's plan matches what I have in mind."

sentences.zh: 乃召見，賜食遣之。

translations.literal: He then summoned [Jing] to audience, granted food, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Jing, gave him a meal, and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 他日，帝又語端。

translations.literal: Another day the Emperor again spoke to Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor spoke to Duan again.

sentences.zh: 曰：「靖說雖是，第田未必墾，課未必入，請下三司雜議。」

translations.literal: saying: "Though Jing's proposal is right, the fields may not necessarily be reclaimed and taxes may not necessarily come in—please refer it to the Three Departments for joint discussion."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Jing may be right, but the land may never be opened and the tax may never arrive—send it to the Three Departments for joint review."

sentences.zh: 於是詔鹽鐵使陳恕等各選判官二人與靖議，以靖為京西勸農使，命大理寺丞皇甫選、光祿寺丞何亮副之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Salt and Iron Commissioner Chen Shu and others each to select two judges to discuss with Jing; Jing was made Commissioner to Encourage Agriculture in the Jingxi Circuit, with Grand Court Judge Huangfu Xuan and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices He Liang as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Salt and Iron Commissioner Chen Shu and others each pick two judges to debate with Jing; Jing became agriculture commissioner for the western capital circuit, with Grand Court Judge Huangfu Xuan and Vice Director He Liang of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices as deputies.

sentences.zh: 選等言其功難成，帝猶謂不然。

translations.literal: Xuan and others said its achievements would be hard to realize, but the Emperor still said otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and the others said success was unlikely, but the emperor still disagreed.

sentences.zh: 既而靖欲假緡錢二萬試行之，陳恕等言：「錢一出，後不能償，則民受害矣。」

translations.literal: Before long Jing wished to borrow twenty thousand strings of cash to trial-run it; Chen Shu and others said: "Once money goes out, if it cannot later be repaid, the people will suffer harm."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jing asked to borrow twenty thousand strings of cash for a trial run; Chen Shu and others said, "Once the money leaves the treasury, if it cannot be recovered the people will bear the loss."

sentences.zh: 帝以群議終不同，始罷之，出靖知婺州，再遷尚書刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: The Emperor, since the group's opinions ultimately differed, at first abandoned it; Jing was sent out as Prefect of Wuzhou, then again promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: With the ministries still divided, the emperor dropped the plan; Jing was sent out as prefect of Wuzhou, then promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，復列前所論勸農事，又言：「國家禦戎西北，而仰食東南，東南食不足，則誤國大計。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, [Jing] again listed his previous proposals on encouraging agriculture, also saying: "The state defends the northwest but relies on food from the southeast; if southeastern food is insufficient, the great plan of the state will be jeopardized.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded, Jing again laid out his farming proposals and said, "The empire guards the northwest but eats from the southeast; if southeastern grain runs short, the whole strategic plan fails.

sentences.zh: 請自京東、西及河北諸州大行勸農之法，以殿最州縣官吏，歲可省江、淮漕百餘萬。」

translations.literal: Request from the eastern and western capital circuits and all prefectures in Hebei to vigorously apply the method of encouraging agriculture, using grades of prefectural and county officials—annually could save over a million piculs of Yangzi-Huai transport."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to extend the farming program through the eastern and western capital circuits and Hebei, grading prefectural and county officials by results—saving more than a million piculs of Yangzi-Huai transport each year."

sentences.zh: 復詔靖條上之，靖請刺史行春，縣令勸耕，孝悌力田者賜爵，置五保以檢察奸盜，籍遊惰之民以供役作。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered Jing to itemize and submit; Jing requested prefects conduct spring inspection tours, magistrates urge plowing, grant ranks to those filial, fraternal, and vigorous in farming, establish five-household units to inspect traitors and bandits, register idle loafers for corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The court again told Jing to draft details: prefects should tour in spring, magistrates urge plowing, grant ranks to the filial and diligent farmers, set up five-household security groups against crime, and register idlers for corvée.

sentences.zh: 又下三司議，皆不果行。

translations.literal: Again referred to the Three Departments for discussion—all ultimately not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: It went back to the Three Departments again, and again nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 歷度支判官，為京畿均田使，出為淮南轉運副使兼發運司公事，徙江南轉運使。

translations.literal: He successively served as judge of the Revenue Office, Commissioner for Equalizing Fields in the Capital Region, sent out as Vice Transport Commissioner of Huainan concurrently in charge of the Tribute Transport Bureau, transferred to Jiangnan Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a revenue judge, then capital-region equal-field commissioner, then vice transport commissioner of Huainan with charge of the tribute transport bureau, and finally Jiangnan transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 極論前李氏橫賦於民凡十七事，詔為罷其尤甚者。

translations.literal: He extensively argued seventeen instances of excessive taxation the former Li regime had imposed on the people; an edict abolished the most egregious among them.
translations.idiomatic: He detailed seventeen kinds of exactions the former Li regime had laid on the people; the court abolished the worst.

sentences.zh: 徙知譚州，歷度支、鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: Transferred to Prefect of Tanzhou, successively Revenue Office and Salt and Iron judge.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Tanzhou as prefect and later served as revenue and salt-and-iron judge.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，為行在三司判官。

translations.literal: On sacrifice at Fenyin, he was Traveling Three Departments judge at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Fenyin sacrifice he was Three Departments judge with the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 又歷京西、京東轉運使，知泉、蘇、越三州，累遷太常少卿，進太僕卿、集賢院學士，知建州，徙泉州，拜左諫訴大夫。

translations.literal: Again successively Jingxi and Jingdong transport commissioner, prefect of Quan, Su, and Yue, repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of Sacrifices, advanced to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, prefect of Jianzhou, transferred to Quanzhou, appointed Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as transport commissioner for the western and eastern capital circuits, governed Quanzhou, Suzhou, and Yuezhou, rose to vice director of sacrifices, then director of the imperial stud and scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, governed Jianzhou and Quanzhou, and was made left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 初，靖與丁謂善，謂貶，黨人皆逐去，提點刑獄、侍御史王耿乃言靖老疾，不宜久為鄉里官，於是以秘書監致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Initially Jing was on good terms with Ding Wei; when Wei was demoted, his faction were all driven away. Judicial Intendant and Palace Censor Wang Geng then said Jing was old and ill and unsuited to long serve as a local official; thereby he retired as Director of the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had once been close to Ding Wei; when Wei fell, his allies were purged. Judicial intendant and palace censor Wang Geng said Jing was old and infirm and should not stay long in a hometown post, so he retired as director of the secretariat and died.

sentences.zh: 靖平生多建畫，而於農事尤詳，嘗取淳化、咸平以來所陳表章，目曰《勸農奏議》，錄上之，然其說泥古，多不可行。

translations.literal: Through life Jing made many plans, especially detailed on agriculture; he once collected memorials submitted from Chunhua and Xianping onward, titled "Memorials on Encouraging Agriculture," and submitted them—but his ideas clung to antiquity and mostly could not be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Jing spent his life proposing reforms, above all on farming; he once gathered his memorials from the Chunhua and Xianping eras into "Memorials on Encouraging Agriculture" and presented them, but his thinking clung to antiquity and much of it could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 張綸，字公信，潁州汝陰人。

translations.literal: Zhang Lun, styled Gongxin, was a native of Ruyin in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun, courtesy name Gongxin, came from Ruyin in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻任氣。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and spirited, free and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and free-spirited.

sentences.zh: 舉進士不中，補三班奉職，遷右班殿直。

translations.literal: He failed the jinshi examination, was made Third Class Attendant, and promoted to Right Class Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the jinshi exam, entered service as a third-class attendant, and rose to right-class palace guard.

sentences.zh: 從雷有終討王均於蜀，有降寇數百據險叛，使綸擊之，綸馳報曰：「此窮寇，急之則生患，不如諭以向背。」

translations.literal: Following Lei Youzhong to suppress Wang Jun in Shu, there were several hundred surrendered bandits occupying dangerous terrain in rebellion; Lun was sent to attack them; Lun galloped back reporting: "These are cornered bandits; pressing them hard will breed trouble—better to instruct them on which side to take."
translations.idiomatic: With Lei Youzhong campaigning against Wang Jun in Shu, several hundred surrendered rebels held rough ground and rose again; Lun was sent against them but rode back saying, "These are desperate men; drive them hard and trouble follows—better explain which side they should join."

sentences.zh: 有終用其說，賊果棄兵來降。

translations.literal: Youzhong adopted his advice; the bandits indeed abandoned arms and came down.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong took his advice, and the rebels laid down their arms and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以功遷右侍禁、慶州兵馬監押，擢閣門祗候，益、彭、簡等州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted Palace Guard of the Right and Supervisor of Bingzhou military horses; selected as Gate Attendant and Commissioner for inspection in Yi, Peng, Jian and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted to right palace guard and supervisor of Bingzhou's military horses, then made gate attendant and chief inspector for Yi, Peng, Jian, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 所部卒縱酒掠居民，綸斬首惡數人，眾乃定。

translations.literal: Troops under his command drunkenly plundered residents; Lun beheaded several ringleaders and the crowd was calmed.
translations.idiomatic: When his troops got drunk and looted civilians, Lun executed several ringleaders and order returned.

sentences.zh: 徙荊湖提點刑獄，遷東頭供奉官、提點開封府界縣鎮公事。

translations.literal: Transferred to judicial intendant of Jinghu and Hubei, promoted Eastern Head Attendant and intendant of counties and towns in the Kaifeng metropolitan district.
translations.idiomatic: He became judicial intendant for Jinghu and Hubei, then eastern head attendant and intendant of counties and towns in the Kaifeng metropolitan zone.

sentences.zh: 奉使靈夏還，會辰州溪峒彭氏蠻內寇，以知辰州。

translations.literal: On return from embassy to Ling and Xia, coinciding with Peng clan of Xi'ong in Chenzhou rebelling inward, [he was appointed] prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from an embassy to Ling and Xia, he was appointed prefect of Chenzhou when the Peng clan of the Xi'ong in Chenzhou raided inward.

sentences.zh: 綸至，築蓬山驛路，賊不得通，乃遁去。

translations.literal: When Lun arrived he built the Pengshan post road; bandits could not get through and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lun built the Pengshan courier road so the rebels could not move freely, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 徙知渭州。

translations.literal: Transferred to prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Weizhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 改內殿崇班、知鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: Changed to Inner Hall Honored Guard and prefect of Zhenyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inner-hall honored guard and prefect of Zhenyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，安撫使曹瑋表留之，不可。

translations.literal: On embassy to the Khitan, Pacification Commissioner Cao Wei memorialized to retain him—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to the Khitan, pacification commissioner Cao Wei asked to keep him at post, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 蠻復入寇，為辰州、澧鼎等州緣邊五溪十峒巡檢安撫使，諭蠻酋禍福，購還所掠民，遣官與盟，刻石於境上。

translations.literal: Bandits again invaded; [he was made] Pacification Commissioner inspecting five streams and ten passes on the border of Chen, Li, Ding and other prefectures; he instructed chieftains on fortune and disaster, offered rewards to return captured people, sent officials to covenant, and carved stone at the border.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes raided again he became pacification commissioner for the five streams and ten passes along the Chen, Li, and Ding borderlands; he warned chiefs of the consequences, paid ransoms for captives, sent officials to swear treaties, and carved the agreement on stone at the frontier.

sentences.zh: 久之，除江、淮制置發運副使。

translations.literal: After long service, appointed Vice Commissioner for the Jiang-Huai Commission arranging tribute transport.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made vice commissioner for Jiang-Huai tribute transport.

sentences.zh: 時鹽課大虧，乃奏除通、泰、楚三州鹽戶宿負，官助其器用，鹽入優與之直，由是歲增課數十萬石。

translations.literal: When salt revenue greatly declined, he memorialized to cancel accumulated debts of salt households in Tong, Tai, and Chu, with government aid for utensils—the state paid salt at favorable prices; thereby annual salt levy increased by hundreds of thousands of piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Salt revenues had collapsed; he memorialized to wipe old debts of salt households in Tong, Tai, and Chu, supply tools from the state, and pay fair prices for salt delivered—adding hundreds of thousands of piculs to the annual levy.

sentences.zh: 復置鹽場於杭、秀、海三州，歲入課又百五十萬。

translations.literal: Salt fields were re-established at Hang, Xiu, and Hai; annual revenue again [increased by] 1.5 million.
translations.idiomatic: He reopened salt works at Hang, Xiu, and Hai, bringing in another 1.5 million in annual revenue.

sentences.zh: 居二歲，增上供米八十萬。

translations.literal: After two years, tribute rice to the capital increased by 800,000.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years he raised tribute rice to the capital by eight hundred thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 疏五渠，導太湖入於海，復租米六十萬。

translations.literal: Five canals were dredged, directing Tai Lake to the sea; recovered rent rice of 600,000.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged five canals to carry Tai Lake water to the sea and recovered six hundred thousand piculs of rent grain.

sentences.zh: 開長蘆西河以避覆舟之患，又築漕河堤二百里於高郵北，旁錮鉅石為十䃮，以泄橫流。

translations.literal: Opened the west branch of Changlu River to avoid capsizing calamity; also built two hundred li of granary canal dikes north of Gaoyou, bracing giant stones into ten sluices to release cross-currents.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the western branch of the Changlu River to reduce shipwrecks, and built two hundred li of canal dikes north of Gaoyou, setting massive stones into ten sluice dams to bleed off cross-currents.

sentences.zh: 泰州有捍海堰，延袤百五十里，久廢不治，歲患海濤冒民田。

translations.literal: Taizhou had a sea-bank dike extending 150 li, long abandoned; each year sea tides flooded civilian fields.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou had a sea wall one hundred fifty li long, long neglected, and every year tides drowned farmland.

sentences.zh: 綸方議修復，論者難之，以為濤患息而畜潦之患興矣。

translations.literal: Lun was just proposing restoration; critics objected, saying when tidal calamity ceased, inland flooding calamity would arise.
translations.idiomatic: Lun proposed rebuilding it, but critics objected that ending tidal flooding would invite inland flooding.

sentences.zh: 綸曰：「濤之患十九，而潦之患十一，獲多而亡少，豈不可邪？」

translations.literal: Lun said: "Tidal calamity is nineteen parts, flooding calamity eleven parts—gaining much with little loss—how can it be wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: Lun replied, "Tidal damage is nine parts in ten; inland flooding is barely one—far more gained than lost. How can that be wrong?"

sentences.zh: 表三請，願身自臨役。

translations.literal: He memorialized three times requesting to personally oversee the labor.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized three times, offering to oversee the work himself.

sentences.zh: 命兼權知泰州，卒成堰，復逋戶二千六百，州民利之，為立生祠。

translations.literal: Ordered to concurrently act as prefect of Taizhou; he completed the dike, restored 2,600 absconded households; the people benefited and erected a living shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed acting prefect of Taizhou, he finished the wall, brought back twenty-six hundred fugitive households, and the people raised a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 居淮南六年，累遷文思使、昭州刺史。

translations.literal: After six years in Huainan, repeatedly promoted to Commissioner of the Office of Literary Endeavor and Prefect of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in Huainan he rose to commissioner of the Office of Literary Endeavor and prefect of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 契丹隆緒死，為吊慰副使。

translations.literal: When Khitan Longxu died, [he was] deputy condolence envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ruler Longxu died, he served as deputy condolence envoy.

sentences.zh: 歷知秦、瀛二州，兩知滄州，再遷東上閣門使，真拜乾州刺史，徙知潁州，卒。

translations.literal: Successively prefect of Qin and Ying, twice prefect of Cang, twice promoted Eastern Upper Gate Attendant, truly appointed Prefect of Gan, transferred to Yingzhou prefect, died.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Qin and Ying, twice governed Cang, rose twice to eastern upper gate attendant, was formally appointed prefect of Gan, moved to Yingzhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 綸有材略，所至興利除害。

translations.literal: Lun had talent and strategy; wherever he went he promoted benefit and removed harm.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was capable and strategic; everywhere he went he advanced public good and removed abuses.

sentences.zh: 為人恕，喜施予，在江、淮，見漕卒凍餒道死者眾，嘆曰：「此有司之過，非所以體上仁也。」

translations.literal: He was forgiving in nature, fond of giving; on the Jiang-Huai he saw many transport troops frozen and starved dead on the roads, sighing: "This is the fault of the officials—not how to embody the court's benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle and generous; on the Jiang-Huai he saw transport workers frozen and starved along the roads and sighed, "This is official negligence, not how to embody the throne's kindness."

sentences.zh: 推奉錢市絮襦千數，衣其不能自存者。

translations.literal: He contributed his salary to buy thousands of cotton padded clothes for those unable to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his salary to buy thousands of padded coats for those who could not survive on their own.

sentences.zh: 邵曄，字日華，其先京兆人。

translations.literal: Shao Ye, styled Rihua—his ancestors were from Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Ye, courtesy name Rihua, came from a Jingzhao family.

sentences.zh: 唐末喪亂，曾祖嶽挈族之荊南謁高季興，不見禮，遂之湖南。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang amid turmoil, his great-grandfather Yue led the clan to Jingnan to visit Gao Jixing, received no courtesy, and went to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tang, in the chaos of collapse, his great-grandfather Yue led the clan to Jingnan to see Gao Jixing, was treated coldly, and moved on to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 彭於刺全州，辟為判官。

translations.literal: When Peng Yu governed Quanzhou he was invited as judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Yu was posted to Quanzhou he took Yue on as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 會賊魯仁恭寇連州，即署嶽國子司業、知州事，遂家桂陽。

translations.literal: When bandit Lu Rengong raided Lianzhou, Yue was appointed Academician of the Directorate of Education and acting prefect; the family settled at Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit Lu Rengong attacked Lianzhou, Yue was made academician of the directorate of education and acting prefect, and the family settled at Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖崇德，道州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chongde was Recording Official of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chongde was recording officer of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 父簡，連山令。

translations.literal: His father Jian was Magistrate of Lianshan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian was magistrate of Lianshan.

sentences.zh: 曄幼嗜學，恥從辟署。

translations.literal: Ye from youth loved learning, ashamed to follow recruitment posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ye loved study from boyhood and disdained taking a post through patronage alone.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，擢進士第，解褐，授邵陽主簿，改大理評事、知蓬州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo, selected jinshi; on leaving mourning appointed Shaoyang Registrar, changed to Grand Court Assessor and Registrar of Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 8 he passed the jinshi examination, left private life, became registrar of Shaoyang, then grand court assessor and recording officer of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 時太子中舍楊全知州，性悍率蒙昧，部民張道豐等三人被誣為劫盜，悉置於死，獄已具，曄察其枉，不署牘，白全當核其實。

translations.literal: At that time Senior Court Attendant Yang Quan was prefect—brutish, coarse, and ignorant; three subjects Zhang Daofeng and others were falsely accused as robbers and all sentenced to death. The case was complete; Ye saw their injustice and would not sign the document, telling Quan the facts should be verified.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was Senior Court Attendant Yang Quan, brutal and crude; three men led by Zhang Daofeng were framed as bandits and sentenced to death. When the file was ready Ye saw the injustice, refused to sign, and told Quan the facts had to be checked.

sentences.zh: 全不聽，引道豐等抵法，號呼不服，再系獄按驗。

translations.literal: Quan would not listen, took Daofeng and others to execution—they cried out in protest; again imprisoned for re-investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Quan ignored him, sent Daofeng and the others to execution—they shouted their innocence—and they were jailed again for reinvestigation.

sentences.zh: 既而捕獲正盜，盜豐等遂得釋，全坐削籍為民。

translations.literal: Soon the real robbers were captured; Daofeng and others were released; Quan was demoted to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the real bandits were caught; Daofeng and the others were freed; Quan was stripped of rank and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 曄代還引對，太宗謂曰：「爾能活吾平民，深可嘉也。」

translations.literal: When Ye returned for audience Taizong said to him: "You were able to save my common people—deeply commendable."
translations.idiomatic: When Ye returned for audience Taizong said, "You saved ordinary people of mine—that is deeply praiseworthy."

sentences.zh: 賜錢五萬，下詔以全事戒諭天下。

translations.literal: Granted fifty thousand cash, issued edict using Quan's case to warn the empire.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him fifty thousand cash and issued an edict using Quan's case to warn officials everywhere.

sentences.zh: 授曄光祿寺丞，使廣南采訪刑獄。

translations.literal: Ye was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and sent to Guangnan to investigate criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and sent to Guangnan to review criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 俄通判荊南，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Soon vice prefect of Jingnan; granted crimson robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was vice prefect of Jingnan and granted the crimson robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 遷著作佐郎、知忠州。

translations.literal: Promoted Assistant Compiler and prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant compiler and made prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷太常丞、江南轉運副使，改監察御史。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Deputy Transport Commissioner of Jiangnan, then was made Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and deputy Jiangnan transport commissioner, then was made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞就養，得知朗州。

translations.literal: Because his mother was aged he requested a nearby post to support her and was appointed prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His mother being old, he asked for a post where he could care for her and was appointed prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 入判三司磨勘司，遷工部員外郎、淮南轉運使。

translations.literal: He entered court to serve as judge of the Three Offices Review Bureau, then was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and Transport Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to judge the Three Offices Review Bureau, then promoted to vice minister of works and Huainan transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 景德中，假光祿卿，充交址安撫國信使。

translations.literal: During the Jingde era he served acting as Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets and was commissioned Pacification Commissioner and State Credentials Envoy to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingde period he acted as director of the Court of Imperial Banquets and was sent to Jiaozhi as pacification commissioner and imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 會黎桓死，其子龍鉞嗣立，兄龍全率兵劫庫財而去，其弟龍廷殺鉞自立，龍廷兄明護率扶蘭砦兵攻戰。

translations.literal: When Li Huan died, his son Long Yue succeeded him; his elder brother Long Quan led troops to loot the treasury and flee; his younger brother Long Ting killed Yue and seized power; Long Ting's elder brother Minghu led troops from the Futlan stockade to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan had just died when his son Long Yue took the throne; an elder brother, Long Quan, led soldiers to plunder the treasury and flee; a younger brother, Long Ting, killed Yue and declared himself ruler; Minghu, another elder brother of Long Ting, then led Futlan garrison troops into battle against him.

sentences.zh: 曄駐嶺表，以事上聞，改命為緣海安撫使，許以便宜設方略。

translations.literal: Ye remained south of the Ling range, reported the situation to the throne, and was reappointed Coastal Pacification Commissioner with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Ye stayed in the Lingnan region, reported events to court, and was reassigned coastal pacification commissioner with discretion to devise strategy on the spot.

sentences.zh: 曄貽書安南，諭朝廷威德，俾速定位。

translations.literal: Ye sent a letter to Annam explaining the court's majesty and virtue and urging them to settle the succession quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Ye wrote to Annam, expounding the dynasty's power and benevolence and urging a swift settlement of who would rule.

sentences.zh: 明護等即時聽命，奉龍廷主軍事。

translations.literal: Minghu and the others immediately obeyed and accepted Long Ting to command military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Minghu and his followers submitted at once and acknowledged Long Ting as military leader.

sentences.zh: 初，詔曄俟其事定，即以黎桓禮物改賜新帥。

translations.literal: Initially the edict instructed Ye that once the matter was settled he should transfer Li Huan's gifts to the new ruler.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court ordered Ye to wait until affairs were settled, then confer on the new ruler the gifts intended for Li Huan.

sentences.zh: 曄上言：「懷撫外夷，當示誠信，不若俟龍廷貢奉，別加封爵而寵賜之。」

translations.literal: Ye memorialized: "In winning over foreign peoples one must show good faith; it would be better to wait until Long Ting sends tribute, then separately grant him a title and bestow honors."
translations.idiomatic: Ye submitted: "To win over outer tribes one must act in good faith; better to wait until Long Ting presents tribute, then grant him a separate title and imperial favor."

sentences.zh: 真宗甚嘉納。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong greatly approved and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong warmly accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 使還，改兵部員外郎，賜金紫。

translations.literal: On returning from the mission he was made Vice Minister of War and granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: When the embassy ended he was promoted to vice minister of war and given the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 初受使，假官錢八十萬，市私覿物，及為安撫，已償其半，餘皆詔除之。

translations.literal: When first commissioned he borrowed eight hundred thousand in official funds to buy private gifts; by the time of the pacification commission he had repaid half, and the remainder was remitted by edict.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the mission he borrowed eight hundred thousand in government funds to purchase personal gifts; by the time he took up the pacification post he had repaid half, and an edict canceled the rest.

sentences.zh: 嘗上《邕州至交州水陸路》及《宜州山川》等四圖，頗詳控制之要。

translations.literal: He once submitted four maps, including "Land and Water Route from Yongzhou to Jiaozhou" and "Mountains and Rivers of Yizhou," detailing key points of control.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented four maps, among them routes by land and water from Yongzhou to Jiaozhou and the mountains and rivers of Yizhou, with considerable detail on how the region could be held.

sentences.zh: 俄判三司三勾院，坐所舉季隨犯贓，曄當削一官，上以其遠使之勤，止令停任。

translations.literal: Soon he was judge of the Three Offices Triple Audit Bureau; because his nominee Ji Sui took bribes Ye should have lost one rank, but the emperor, for his diligence on the distant mission, only suspended him from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to the Three Offices Triple Audit Bureau; when a man he had recommended, Ji Sui, was convicted of graft Ye should have been demoted one rank, but the emperor, mindful of his arduous service abroad, merely suspended him from duty.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，起知兗州，表請東封，優詔答之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was recalled as prefect of Yanzhou, memorialized requesting the eastern feng, and received a gracious edict in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong Xiangfu he was recalled to serve as prefect of Yanzhou, petitioned for an eastern feng rite, and received a warm imperial response.

sentences.zh: 及遣王欽若、趙安仁經度封禪，仍判州事，就命曄為京東轉運使。

translations.literal: When Wang Qinruo and Zhao Anren were dispatched to plan the feng and shan rites, Ye still judged prefectural affairs and was concurrently appointed Jingdong Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qinruo and Zhao Anren were sent to oversee the feng and shan ceremonies, Ye continued to administer the prefecture and was at the same time made Jingdong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 封禪禮畢，超拜刑部郎中，復判三勾院，出為淮南、江、浙、荊湖制置發運使。

translations.literal: When the feng and shan rites were finished he was promoted beyond precedent to Director of the Ministry of Justice, again judged the Triple Audit Bureau, then went out as Commissioner for Prepared Grain Transport of Huainan, Jiang, Zhe, and Jinghu.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites he was promoted ahead of schedule to director of the Ministry of Justice, served again in the Triple Audit Bureau, and then became commissioner for prepared grain transport across Huainan, Jiang, Zhe, and Jinghu.

sentences.zh: 四年，改右諫議大夫、知廣州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Right Remonstrating Grandee and prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed right remonstrating grandee and prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 州城瀕海，每蕃舶至岸，常苦颶風，曄鑿內濠通舟，颶不能害。

translations.literal: The prefectural city stood on the coast; whenever foreign ships reached shore they often suffered from typhoons; Ye dug an inner moat so boats could pass through, and the typhoons could no longer harm them.
translations.idiomatic: The city lay on the sea, and foreign vessels that made port were often wrecked by typhoons; Ye cut an inner channel so ships could shelter inside, and the storms no longer did damage.

sentences.zh: 俄遘疾卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill and died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took ill and died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 崔立，字本之，開封鄢陵人。

translations.literal: Cui Li, styled Benzhi, was a native of Yanling in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Li, courtesy name Benzhi, came from Yanling in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 祖周度，仕周為泰寧軍節度判官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhou Du served the Later Zhou as military judge of the Taining Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhou Du had served the Later Zhou as military judge on the Taining circuit.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超叛，周度以大義責之，遂見殺。

translations.literal: When Murong Yanchao rebelled, Zhou Du rebuked him on grounds of righteousness and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Yanchao rose in rebellion, Zhou Du condemned him on principle and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 立中進士第。

translations.literal: Li passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Li passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 為果州團練推官，役兵輦官物，道險，乃率眾錢，傭舟載歸。

translations.literal: As aide to the Guozhou militia commission, corvée soldiers were hauling official goods; the road was dangerous, so he collected money from the men and hired boats to carry the goods back.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as aide on the Guozhou militia commission, he saw corvée troops hauling government freight over a perilous route; he pooled their funds and hired boats to transport the cargo instead.

sentences.zh: 知州姜從革論如率斂法，當斬三人，立曰：「此非私己，罪杖爾。」

translations.literal: Prefect Jiang Congge argued that this resembled illegal levying and that three men should be executed; Li said: "This was not for private gain—the punishment should be beating with the rod."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Jiang Congge held that the act amounted to unlawful exaction and that three men should die; Li replied, "They did not enrich themselves—the offense warrants the rod alone."

sentences.zh: 從革初不聽，卒論奏，詔如立議。

translations.literal: Congge at first would not listen, but in the end the case was reported upward and an edict followed Li's view.
translations.idiomatic: Congge refused at first, but the matter was eventually reported to court and an edict adopted Li's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 真宗記之，特改大理寺丞，知安豐縣。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong took note and specially promoted him to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and made him magistrate of Anfeng County.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong remembered the case and specially made him assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Anfeng County.

sentences.zh: 大水壞期斯塘，立躬督繕治，逾月而成。

translations.literal: Great floods destroyed the Qisi embankment; Li personally supervised repairs, and within a month it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: When a great flood breached the Qisi embankment, Li personally oversaw the repairs and completed them in little more than a month.

sentences.zh: 進殿中丞，歷通判廣州、許州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and served in succession as vice prefect of Guangzhou and Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to palace attendant, he served successively as vice prefect of Guangzhou and Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會滑州塞決河，調民出芻楗，命立提舉受納。

translations.literal: When Huazhou was closing a breached river, the people were levied for fodder and fascines; Li was ordered to supervise collection.
translations.idiomatic: When Huazhou was sealing a river breach, the populace was called on for fodder and fascines, and Li was put in charge of receiving the supplies.

sentences.zh: 立計其用有餘，而下戶未輸者尚二百萬，悉奏弛之。

translations.literal: Li calculated that the need had already been met, yet lower households still owed two million; he memorialized to remit it all.
translations.idiomatic: Li reckoned that enough had been collected while poorer households still owed two million; he memorialized and had the entire remainder waived.

sentences.zh: 知江陰軍，屬縣有利港久廢，立教民浚治，既成，溉田數千頃，及開橫河六十里，通運漕。

translations.literal: As prefect of Jiangyin Army, a subordinate county had the long-abandoned Lijin Harbor; Li instructed the people to dredge it; when finished it irrigated several thousand qing of fields, and he also opened a transverse canal sixty li long to connect grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: As military prefect of Jiangyin he found Lijin Harbor in a subordinate county long neglected; he had the people dredge it, and when the work was done it irrigated thousands of qing of farmland; he also cut a lateral canal sixty li long to link the transport routes.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常少卿，歷知棣、漢、相、潞、兗、鄆、涇七州。

translations.literal: He rose in stages to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and served in succession as prefect of Di, Han, Xiang, Lu, Yan, Yun, and Jing—seven prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and governed in turn Di, Han, Xiang, Lu, Yan, Yun, and Jing—seven prefectures in all.

sentences.zh: 兗州歲大饑，募富人出谷十萬餘石振餓者，所全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: In Yanzhou a year of great famine came; he urged the wealthy to contribute more than one hundred thousand shi of grain to relieve the starving, and very many lives were saved.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhou suffered a severe famine he persuaded wealthy households to donate more than one hundred thousand shi of grain to feed the hungry, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 立性淳謹，尤喜論事。

translations.literal: Li's nature was plain and careful, and he especially liked to discuss affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Li was sincere and cautious by nature and especially fond of speaking out on public matters.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符間，帝既封禪，士大夫爭奏上符瑞，獻贊頌，立獨言：「水發徐州，旱連江、淮，無為烈風，金陵火，天所以警驕惰、戒淫泆也，區區符瑞，尚何足為治道言哉？」

translations.literal: During Dazhong Xiangfu, after the emperor had performed the feng and shan rites, scholar-officials vied to report auspicious signs and offer panegyrics; Li alone said: "Floods rose at Xuzhou, drought ran through the Jiang and Huai regions, a violent wind struck Wuyang, and fire broke out at Jinling—these are heaven's warnings against pride and sloth and admonitions against excess; what are petty omens worth saying about the way of governance?"
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong Xiangfu era, after the emperor's feng and shan rites, officials competed to report portents and submit praise; Li alone argued, "Floods at Xuzhou, drought across the Jiang and Huai, a fierce wind at Wuyang, fire at Jinling—these are heaven's warnings against arrogance and indulgence; what can petty omens possibly tell us about good government?"

sentences.zh: 前後上四十餘事。

translations.literal: In all he submitted more than forty such memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Over time he submitted more than forty such memorials.

sentences.zh: 以右諫議大夫知耀州，改知濠州，遷給事中。

translations.literal: As Right Remonstrating Grandee he was prefect of Yaozhou, then transferred to Haozhou, and was promoted to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served as right remonstrating grandee and prefect of Yaozhou, then was moved to Haozhou and promoted to attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 告老，進尚書工部侍郎致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on account of age, was advanced to Vice Minister of Works in the Ministry of Revenue with permission to retire, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire, was promoted to vice minister of works in the Ministry of Revenue and granted leave to withdraw from office, then died.

sentences.zh: 識韓琦於布衣，以女妻之，人嘗服其鑒雲。

translations.literal: He recognized Han Qi while Qi was still in plain clothes and gave him his daughter in marriage; people often admired his discernment.
translations.idiomatic: He spotted Han Qi's talent before Qi had risen in the world and gave him his daughter in marriage; people long admired his eye for men.

sentences.zh: 魯有開，字元翰，參知政事宗道從子也。

translations.literal: Lu Youkai, styled Yuanhan, was a nephew of Associate Administrator Zongdao.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Youkai, courtesy name Yuanhan, was a nephew of the associate administrator Lu Zongdao.

sentences.zh: 好《禮》學，通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He loved the study of the Rites and was thoroughly versed in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to ritual learning and mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 用宗道蔭，知韋城縣。

translations.literal: Through Zongdao's yin privilege he became magistrate of Weicheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through Zongdao's hereditary privilege and became magistrate of Weicheng County.

sentences.zh: 曹、濮劇盜橫行旁縣間，聞其名不敢入境。

translations.literal: Fierce bandits ran rampant between Cao and Pu and neighboring counties, but hearing his name they did not dare enter his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Violent bandits terrorized the counties around Cao and Pu, yet at the sound of his name they would not cross into his district.

sentences.zh: 知確山縣，大姓把持官政，有開治其最甚者，遂以無事。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Queshan County, powerful clans controlled local government; Youkai punished the worst offenders, and thereafter there was peace.
translations.idiomatic: At Queshan County great families had seized control of local affairs; Youkai dealt with the worst of them, and the district thereafter stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 興廢陂，溉民田數千頃。

translations.literal: He restored abandoned reservoirs and irrigated several thousand qing of the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt derelict irrigation works and watered several thousand qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 富弼守蔡，薦之，以為有古循吏風。

translations.literal: When Fu Bi governed Cai Prefecture he recommended him, saying he had the bearing of the virtuous officials of old.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Cai, Fu Bi recommended him, declaring that he had the spirit of the virtuous officials of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 知金州，有蠱獄，當死者數十人，有開曰：「欲殺人，衷謀之足矣，安得若是眾邪？」

translations.literal: As prefect of Jinzhou there was a witchcraft case with dozens facing death; Youkai said: "If one wished to kill, a few conspirators would suffice—how could there be so many?"
translations.idiomatic: While prefect of Jinzhou he faced a witchcraft case in which dozens were sentenced to die; Youkai said, "If the aim was murder, a handful of plotters would be enough—how could the guilty be so numerous?"

sentences.zh: 訊之則誣。

translations.literal: On interrogation it proved false.
translations.idiomatic: Under questioning the charges proved false.

sentences.zh: 天方旱，獄白而雨。

translations.literal: Heaven was then in drought; when the case was cleared, rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: A drought was then afflicting the land; when the prisoners were cleared, rain came.

sentences.zh: 知南康軍，代還。

translations.literal: He was military prefect of Nankang and returned when his term ended.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military prefect of Nankang and returned when his replacement arrived.

sentences.zh: 熙寧行新法，王安石問江南如何，曰：「法新行，未見其患，當在異日也。」

translations.literal: When the Xining New Policies were enacted, Wang Anshi asked how things were in Jiangnan; he replied: "The laws have only just been put in force—the harm is not yet visible; it will come later."
translations.idiomatic: When the Xining reforms began, Wang Anshi asked how Jiangnan was faring; Youkai answered, "The new laws have only just taken effect—the trouble is not yet apparent; it will show itself in time."

sentences.zh: 以所對乖異，出通判杭州。

translations.literal: Because this answer diverged from the expected line, he was sent out as vice prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because his reply ran counter to official expectations, he was posted out as vice prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 知衛州，水災，人乏食，擅貸常平錢粟與之，且奏乞蠲其息。

translations.literal: As prefect of Weizhou, when flood disaster struck and people lacked food, he on his own authority lent them Ever-Normal Granary funds and grain and also memorialized asking that interest be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Weizhou, when floods left people without food, he on his own authority drew on Ever-Normal Granary funds and grain to lend to them and memorialized to cancel the interest.

sentences.zh: 徙冀州，增堤，或謂：「郡無水患，何以役為？」

translations.literal: Transferred to Jizhou, he raised the dikes; someone said: "The commandery has no flood trouble—why impose corvée labor?"
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Jizhou, he raised the dikes; some asked, "This prefecture has no history of flooding—why call out labor?"

sentences.zh: 有開曰：「豫備不虞，古之善計也。」

translations.literal: Youkai said: "To prepare against the unforeseen is a sound plan of old."
translations.idiomatic: Youkai replied, "To guard against the unexpected is an ancient and wise policy."

sentences.zh: 卒成之。

translations.literal: In the end the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The project was completed in the end.

sentences.zh: 明年河決，水果至，不能冒堤而止。

translations.literal: The next year the Yellow River breached its banks; floodwaters arrived but could not surmount the dikes and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Yellow River broke its banks; the flood came but could not climb over the dikes and was halted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使河北，民遮誦有開功狀，召為膳部郎中，元祐中，歷知信陽軍、洺滑州，復守冀，官至中大夫，卒。

translations.literal: When the court sent envoys to Hebei, the people blocked the road to recite Youkai's achievements; he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Rites for Provisions; during the Yuanyou era he served in succession as military prefect of Xinyang and prefect of Ming and Hua, again guarded Ji, rose to Grandee of the Palace, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial envoys traveled through Hebei, the people stopped them to praise Youkai's record of service; he was recalled as director in the Ministry of Rites for provisions; in the Yuanyou period he governed Xinyang and Ming-Hua in turn, returned to Ji, reached grandee of the palace, and died.

sentences.zh: 張逸，字大隱，鄭州滎陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, styled Dayin, was a native of Xingyang in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Dayin, came from Xingyang in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，為試秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was made a probationary collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the jinshi examination, he became a probationary collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 知襄州鄧城縣，有能名。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Dengcheng County in Xiangzhou he gained a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Dengcheng in Xiangzhou he earned a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 積州謝泌將薦逸，先設几案，置章其上，望闕再拜曰：「老臣為朝廷得一良吏。」

translations.literal: Prefect Xie Bi was about to recommend Yi; he first set out a desk, placed the memorial upon it, bowed twice toward the palace, and said: "This old servant has found the court a worthy official."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Bi, the prefect, was about to recommend Yi; he set out a desk, laid the memorial on it, bowed twice toward the palace, and said, "Your old servant has secured a fine official for the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 乃奏之。

translations.literal: Then he submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Then he sent in the memorial.

sentences.zh: 他日引對，真宗問所欲何官，逸對曰：「母老在家，願得近鄉一幕職官，歸奉甘旨足矣。」

translations.literal: On another day he was summoned for audience; Zhenzong asked what office he desired; Yi replied: "My mother is old at home; I wish only a local staff post near my home county so I may return and provide for her—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: On a later audience day Emperor Zhenzong asked what post he wanted; Yi answered, "My mother is old and at home; I ask only for a county staff appointment near my native place so I can go back and support her—that is all I want."

sentences.zh: 授澶州觀察推官，數日，以母喪去。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating officer on the Chanzong observation commission; within days he left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the post of investigating officer on the Chanzong observation commission; within days he resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，引對，帝又固問之，對曰：「願得京官。」

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned again; the emperor pressed the question once more, and he replied: "I wish to receive a capital appointment."
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he was called in again; the emperor pressed him once more, and he replied, "I would like a capital appointment."

sentences.zh: 特改大理寺丞。

translations.literal: He was specially made Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 帝雅賢泌，再召問逸者，用泌薦也。

translations.literal: The emperor had long esteemed Bi and summoned Yi again to question him because of Bi's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always held Bi in high regard and questioned Yi again on Bi's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 知長水縣，時王嗣宗留守西京，厚遇之，及徙青神縣，貧不自給，嗣宗假奉半年使辦裝。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Changshui County, Wang Sizong was then regent at the Western Capital and treated him generously; when Yi was transferred to Qingshen County he was too poor to support himself, and Sizong lent him half a year's salary to prepare for the move.
translations.idiomatic: While magistrate of Changshui, he enjoyed the warm patronage of Wang Sizong, regent of the Western Capital; when he was moved to Qingshen he could barely support himself, and Sizong advanced him half a year's salary for travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 既至縣，興學校，教生徒。

translations.literal: Once he reached the county he established schools and instructed students.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the county he founded schools and taught students.

sentences.zh: 後邑人陳希亮、楊異相繼登科，逸改其居曰桂枝裏。

translations.literal: Later townspeople Chen Xiliang and Yang Yi passed the examinations in succession, and Yi renamed his residence Gui Branch Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Later two local men, Chen Xiliang and Yang Yi, passed the examinations in turn, and Yi renamed his home Gui Branch Lane.

sentences.zh: 縣東南有松柏灘，夏秋暴漲多覆舟，逸禱江神，不逾月，灘為徙五里，時人異之。

translations.literal: Southeast of the county was Songbai Shoal; in summer and autumn sudden floods often capsized boats; Yi prayed to the river god, and in less than a month the shoal shifted five li—people of the time marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the county lay Songbai Shoal, where summer and autumn floods often sank boats; Yi prayed to the river god, and within a month the shoal had shifted five li—a wonder to all who heard of it.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常博士、知尉氏縣。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and made magistrate of Weishi County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed magistrate of Weishi County.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史，提點益州路刑獄，開封府判官。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Investigating Censor, Intendant of Criminal Cases on the Yizhou Circuit, and judge of the Kaifeng Prefecture office.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to investigating censor, intendant of criminal cases on the Yizhou circuit, and judge in the Kaifeng prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，為兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as envoy to the Khitan and became Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: He went on embassy to the Khitan and later became transport commissioner of the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 徙陜西，未赴，又徙河東，居數月，復徙陜西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shaanxi; before he took up the post he was transferred again to Hedong; after several months he was transferred back to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Shaanxi, reassigned to Hedong before he could take up the post, and after a few months sent back to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 以龍圖閣待制知梓州。

translations.literal: As Drafting Attendant at the Hall of Dragon Illustrations he was made prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: With the title drafting attendant at the Hall of Dragon Illustrations he became prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書兵部郎中，知開封府。

translations.literal: He rose in stages to Director in the Ministry of War in the Ministry of Revenue and was made prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to director in the Ministry of War and appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 有僧求內降免田稅，而逸固執不許。

translations.literal: A monk sought an internal edict exempting him from field tax, but Yi firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: A monk petitioned for an imperial exemption from land tax, but Yi steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「有司能守法，朕何憂也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said: "When officials can uphold the law, what have I to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong said, "When the bureaucracy keeps the law, what need have I to worry?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「頃禁命婦幹禁中恩，比來稍通女謁，願令官司糾劾。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Recently consorts of officials were forbidden to solicit favors within the palace; of late women have again been gaining access through petitions—I ask that the offices investigate and punish this."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Consorts of officials were recently barred from seeking favors inside the palace, yet lately such petitions have crept back in; I ask that the offices investigate and prosecute them."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 以樞密直學士知益州。

translations.literal: As Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs he was made prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs he became prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 逸凡四至蜀，諳其民風。

translations.literal: Yi had gone to Shu four times in all and knew its customs well.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had been to Shu four times in all and knew its people and customs intimately.

sentences.zh: 華陽騶長殺人，誣道旁行者，縣吏受財，獄既具，乃使殺人者守囚。

translations.literal: A Huayang stable chief murdered someone and framed a passerby on the road; county clerks took bribes; when the case was complete they even made the murderer guard the prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: A stable chief in Huayang killed a man and framed a traveler on the road; county clerks took bribes, and when the case was closed they put the actual killer in charge of guarding the prisoner.

sentences.zh: 逸曰：「囚色冤，守者氣不直，豈守者殺人乎？」

translations.literal: Yi said: "The prisoner looks wronged, and the guard's bearing is not upright—could the guard be the killer?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The prisoner looks aggrieved, and the guard's manner is guilty—could the guard be the murderer?"

sentences.zh: 囚始敢言，而守者果服，立誅之，蜀人以為神。

translations.literal: Only then did the prisoner dare speak; the guard indeed confessed, was immediately executed, and the people of Shu regarded Yi as divine.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the prisoner dare speak out; the guard confessed, was executed at once, and the people of Shu thought Yi almost supernatural.

sentences.zh: 會歲旱，逸使作堰壅江水，溉民田，自出公租減價以振民。

translations.literal: When drought struck that year, Yi had a weir built to dam the river and irrigate the people's fields, and from his own official rent he cut prices to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought drought; Yi had a weir built to hold back river water and irrigate farmland, and from his own official income he sold grain at reduced prices to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 初，民饑多殺耕牛食之，犯者皆配關中。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the people were hungry many slaughtered plow oxen for food; offenders were all exiled to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in famine years many peasants had killed draft oxen for food, and offenders were all banished to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 逸奏：「民殺牛以活將死之命，與盜殺者異，若不禁之，又將廢穡事。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized: "When people kill oxen to save lives on the verge of death, it differs from killing oxen by theft; if it is not forbidden, farming will again be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Yi memorialized, "Peasants who slaughter oxen to stave off starvation are not the same as thieves who steal and kill cattle; yet if the practice is unchecked, agriculture will collapse.

sentences.zh: 今歲少稔，請一切放還，復其業。」

translations.literal: This year the harvest is somewhat good; I ask that all such offenders be released and restored to their occupations."
translations.idiomatic: This year the harvest is fair; I ask that all such exiles be pardoned and sent home to resume farming."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒於官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he died in office.

sentences.zh: 吳遵路，字安道。

translations.literal: Wu Zunlu, styled Andao.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zunlu, courtesy name Andao.

sentences.zh: 父淑，見《文苑傳》。

translations.literal: His father Shu is treated in the "Biographies of Men of Letters."
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu has a biography in the "Men of Letters" section.

sentences.zh: 第進士，累官至殿中丞，為秘閣校理。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, rose in stages to Palace Attendant, and served as collator at the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, rose through the ranks to palace attendant, and served as collator in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后稱制，政事得失，下莫敢言。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian held the regency, none below dared speak of the rights and wrongs of government.
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Dowager Zhangxian ruled as regent, no one dared speak openly about what was going wrong in government.

sentences.zh: 遵路條奏十餘事，語皆切直，忤太后意，出知常州。

translations.literal: Zunlu submitted a memorial listing more than ten matters; his language was all incisive and direct, offending the Empress Dowager's wishes, and he was sent out as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zunlu submitted a memorial setting forth more than ten matters in language that was blunt and forthright, offending the Empress Dowager and earning his dismissal to serve as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗預市米吳中，以備歲儉，已而果大乏食，民賴以濟，自他州流至者亦全十八九。

translations.literal: Once he pre-purchased rice in Wu to prepare for a lean year; afterward there indeed was a great shortage of food, and the people relied on it for relief; of those who flowed in from other prefectures, eight or nine tenths were also saved.
translations.idiomatic: He had once bought up rice in advance in the Wu region against a coming lean year, and when famine did strike the people were saved by those stores; refugees who poured in from other prefectures were preserved as well, eight or nine out of ten of them.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書司封員外郎，權開封府推官，改三司鹽鐵判官，加直史館，為淮南轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments in the Ministry of Revenue, acting judicial officer of the Kaifeng prefecture, transferred to be salt-and-iron commissioner of the Three Fiscal Offices, given concurrent appointment in the Historiography Institute, and made deputy transport commissioner for Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he became vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's Bureau of Appointments, served as acting judicial officer in Kaifeng, was transferred to salt-and-iron commissioner in the Three Fiscal Offices, given a concurrent post in the Historiography Institute, and appointed deputy transport commissioner for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 會罷江、淮發運使，遂兼發運司事。

translations.literal: At a time when the Jiang-Huai transport commissioner had been abolished, he thus also took charge of transport administration.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiang-Huai transport commissioner was abolished, he took on the duties of the transport administration as well.

sentences.zh: 嘗於真楚泰州、高郵軍置斗門十九，以畜泄水利。

translations.literal: Once at Taizhou of Zhenchu and Gaoyou Military Prefecture he set up nineteen sluice gates for storing and releasing water for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizhou in Zhenchu and at Gaoyou Military Prefecture he built nineteen sluice gates to hold and release water for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 又廣屬郡常平倉儲畜至二百萬，以待凶歲。

translations.literal: He also expanded the ever-normal granaries of subordinate prefectures, storing up to two million, to await famine years.
translations.idiomatic: He also enlarged the ever-normal granaries in the prefectures under his jurisdiction until they held two million units of grain, set aside against famine years.

sentences.zh: 凡所規畫，後皆便之。

translations.literal: Every measure he planned and organized was afterward found convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Every project he planned proved useful in the years that followed.

sentences.zh: 遷工部郎中，坐失按蘄州王蒙正故入部吏死罪，降知洪州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works; because he failed to investigate properly the case in which Wang Mengzheng of Qizhou had intentionally caused a department clerk to receive the death penalty, he was demoted and made prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director in the Ministry of Works, he was demoted to prefect of Hongzhou for failing to investigate properly the case in which Wang Mengzheng of Qizhou had deliberately framed a department clerk for a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 徙廣州，辭不行。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangzhou, but declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guangzhou but declined the appointment and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 是時發運司既復置使，乃以為發運使，未至，召修起居註。

translations.literal: At this time, since the transport administration had restored the commissioner, he was appointed transport commissioner; before he arrived, he was recalled to compile the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: The transport administration had by then restored the office of commissioner, and he was appointed to that post; before he could take up the assignment, however, he was recalled to compile the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，建請復民兵。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he submitted a proposal requesting restoration of the militia.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he proposed restoring the militia.

sentences.zh: 除天章閣待制、河東路計置糧草。

translations.literal: He was appointed as awaited appointee in the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and tasked with provisioning grain and fodder on the Hedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an awaited appointee in the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and charged with provisioning grain and fodder on the Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 受詔料揀河東鄉民可為兵者，諸路視以為法。

translations.literal: He received an order to assess and select village people in Hedong who could serve as soldiers; all circuits took this as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to assess and select village men in Hedong fit for military service, he carried out the task in a way that other circuits took as their model.

sentences.zh: 進兵部郎中、權知開封府，馭吏嚴肅，屬縣無追逮。

translations.literal: Promoted to Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting prefect of Kaifeng, he controlled officials with stern severity, and in subordinate counties there was no need for pursuit and arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director in the Ministry of War and made acting prefect of Kaifeng, he kept his subordinates under strict discipline, and in the counties under his jurisdiction there was scarcely any need to hunt down offenders.

sentences.zh: 時宋庠、鄭戩、葉清臣皆宰相呂夷簡所不悅，遵路與三人雅相厚善，夷簡忌之，出知宣州。

translations.literal: At the time Song Qi, Zheng Yan, and Ye Qingchen were all disliked by the chief councilor Lü Yijian; Zunlu was on close terms with all three; Yijian resented him and sent him out as prefect of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qi, Zheng Yan, and Ye Qingchen were all out of favor with Chief Councilor Lü Yijian, and Zunlu was on intimate terms with all three; Yijian resented this and had him sent out as prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 上《禦戎要略》、《邊防雜事》二十篇。

translations.literal: He submitted "Essentials for Defense against Barbarians" and "Miscellaneous Matters on Border Defense," twenty chapters in all.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted two works, "Essentials for Defense against Barbarians" and "Miscellaneous Matters on Border Defense," twenty chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 徙陜西都轉運使，遷龍圖閣直學士、知永興軍，被病猶決事不輟，手自作奏。

translations.literal: Transferred to chief transport commissioner for Shaanxi, promoted to academician at the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and made military prefect of Yongxing; though ill he still decided cases without pause, personally writing his memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to chief transport commissioner for Shaanxi and promoted to academician in the Hall of Dragon Diagrams as military prefect of Yongxing, he continued to decide cases without interruption even while ill, drafting his own memorials by hand.

sentences.zh: 及卒，仁宗聞而悼之，詔遣官護喪還京師。

translations.literal: When he died, Renzong heard and mourned him, ordering officials to escort the bier back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Emperor Renzong mourned him on hearing the news and ordered officials to escort his coffin back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 遵路幼聰敏，既長，博學知大體。

translations.literal: Zunlu was clever and quick as a child; once grown, he was broadly learned and grasped the larger pattern of things.
translations.idiomatic: Zunlu was bright and quick-witted as a boy, and when he grew up he became broadly learned and understood affairs in their larger scope.

sentences.zh: 母喪，廬墓蔬食終制。

translations.literal: On his mother's death, he lived by the grave eating plain food until the mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he lived in a hut by her grave on plain food until the full mourning period was complete.

sentences.zh: 性夷雅慎重，寡言笑，善筆劄。

translations.literal: His nature was calm, refined, and cautious; he spoke and laughed little, and was skilled at writing letters.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was mild, dignified, and careful; he spoke and laughed little, and he wrote excellent letters.

sentences.zh: 其為政簡易不為聲威，立朝敢言，無所阿倚。

translations.literal: In governing he was simple and easy, not relying on display of authority; in court he spoke boldly, leaning on no one.
translations.idiomatic: In office he governed simply and without ostentatious show of authority; at court he spoke boldly and leaned on no faction.

sentences.zh: 平居廉儉無他好，既沒，室無長物，其友范仲淹分奉赒其家。
