translations.literal: In ordinary life he was frugal and sparing with no other indulgences; when he died his household had nothing to spare; his friend Fan Zhongyan shared his salary to provide for the family.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he was frugal and had no other pursuits; when he died his home held scarcely anything, and his friend Fan Zhongyan shared his salary to support the family.

sentences.zh: 子瑛，為尚書比部員外郎，不待老而歸。

translations.literal: His son Ying served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Comparisons in the Ministry of Revenue and retired before reaching the age for retirement.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying served as vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's Bureau of Comparisons and retired before he was old enough to do so by rule.

sentences.zh: 趙尚寬，字濟之，河南人，參知政事安仁子也。

translations.literal: Zhao Shangkuan, styled Jizhi, was a man of Henan, son of the Vice Grand Councilor Anren.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shangkuan, courtesy name Jizhi, was a native of Henan and the son of Vice Grand Councilor Anren.

sentences.zh: 知平陽縣。

translations.literal: He was magistrate of Pingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Pingyang County.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑有大囚十數，破械夜逸，殺居民，將犯境，尚寬趣尉出捕，曰：「盜謂我不能來，方怠惰，易取也。

translations.literal: In a neighboring county there were more than ten major convicts who broke their shackles and fled by night, killed residents, and were about to cross the border; Shangkuan urged the constable to go out and capture them, saying: "The bandits think I cannot come; they are just now slack and idle — easy to take.
translations.idiomatic: In a neighboring county more than ten major convicts broke their shackles and fled by night, killing residents and heading toward his border; Shangkuan urged the constable to go out after them, saying, "The robbers think I cannot come — they are slack and off guard now, and easy to take.

sentences.zh: 宜亟往，毋使得散漫，且為害。」

translations.literal: You should go quickly, and not let them scatter and cause harm."
translations.idiomatic: Go at once, before they scatter and do further harm."

sentences.zh: 尉既出，又遣僥巡兵躡其後，悉獲之。

translations.literal: Once the constable had gone out, he also sent patrol soldiers to follow in their tracks, and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: After the constable set out, he also sent patrol troops to follow in their tracks, and all of the fugitives were captured.

sentences.zh: 知忠州，俗畜蠱殺人，尚寬揭方書市中，教人服藥，募索為蠱者窮治，置於理，大化其俗。

translations.literal: As prefect of Zhongzhou, where the custom was to keep gu poisons to kill people, Shangkuan posted prescriptions in the market, taught people to take medicine, offered rewards to seek out gu-makers and punish them severely, and greatly transformed local custom.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Zhongzhou, where the custom was to keep gu poisons for killing people, he posted prescriptions in the market, taught people how to take antidotes, offered rewards to hunt down gu-makers and punish them to the full extent of the law, and in this way greatly changed local ways.

sentences.zh: 轉運使持鹽數十萬斤，譚民易白金，期會促，尚寬發官帑所儲副其須，徐與民為市，不擾而集。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner held several hundred thousand jin of salt and required the people to exchange it for silver; the deadline was urgent; Shangkuan drew on government funds in store to meet the need, then gradually traded with the people, and it was collected without disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner held several hundred thousand jin of salt and demanded that the people exchange it for silver; the deadline was tight, so Shangkuan drew on government reserves to meet the immediate need and then traded with the people at an orderly pace, collecting the salt without causing unrest.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，以考課第一知唐州。

translations.literal: During the Jiayou era, on top examination ranking he became prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou reign period he was appointed prefect of Tangzhou after ranking first in his performance evaluation.

sentences.zh: 唐素沃壤，經五代亂，田不耕，土曠民稀，賦不足以充役，議者欲廢為邑。

translations.literal: Tang had always been fertile land; having suffered the turmoil of the Five Dynasties, fields went unplowed, land lay fallow and people were sparse, and taxes were insufficient to meet corvée obligations; counselors wished to abolish it as a prefecture and reduce it to a county.
translations.idiomatic: Tangzhou had always been rich land, but after the chaos of the Five Dynasties its fields went untilled, its land lay empty and its people were few, and its tax revenue could not even meet corvée obligations; some officials proposed abolishing the prefecture and reducing it to a county.

sentences.zh: 尚寬曰：「土曠可益墾辟，民稀可益招徠，何廢郡之有？」

translations.literal: Shangkuan said: "Fallow land can be further opened to cultivation; sparse population can be further drawn in — why abolish the prefecture?"
translations.idiomatic: Shangkuan said, "Empty land can be opened further to cultivation, and a sparse population can be drawn in — why abolish the prefecture?"

sentences.zh: 乃按視圖記，得漢召信臣陂渠故跡，益發卒復疏三陂一渠，溉田萬餘頃。

translations.literal: He then examined maps and records, found the old traces of Han-era Zhaoxin Chen's dikes and channels, additionally dispatched laborers to reopen three reservoirs and one canal, and irrigated more than ten thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He then consulted maps and records, found the old traces of the Han official Zhaoxin Chen's reservoirs and channels, sent out more laborers to reopen three reservoirs and one canal, and irrigated more than ten thousand qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 又教民自為支渠數十，轉相浸灌。

translations.literal: He also taught the people to dig dozens of branch channels themselves, irrigating in relay.
translations.idiomatic: He also taught the people to dig dozens of branch channels themselves, linking them in sequence for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 而四方之民來者雲布，尚寬復請以荒田計口授之，及貸民官錢買耕牛。

translations.literal: And as people came from all quarters thick as clouds, Shangkuan again requested that wasteland be allotted by head count, and that official funds be lent to the people to buy plow oxen.
translations.idiomatic: As settlers poured in from all directions like clouds gathering, Shangkuan further requested that wasteland be allotted by head count and that government funds be lent to the people to buy plow oxen.

sentences.zh: 比三年，榛莽復為膏腴，增戶積萬餘。

translations.literal: Within three years, thicket and scrub became rich soil again; added households totaled more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years thicket and scrubland had become rich farmland again, and more than ten thousand new households had been added.

sentences.zh: 尚寬勤於農政，治有異等之效，三司使包拯與部使者交上其事，仁宗聞而嘉之，下詔褒焉，仍進秩賜金。

translations.literal: Shangkuan was diligent in agricultural administration, and his governance had extraordinary effects; Fiscal Commissioner Bao Zheng and circuit envoys jointly reported the matter upward; Renzong heard and commended it, issuing an edict of praise, and moreover promoting his rank and bestowing gold.
translations.idiomatic: Shangkuan was tireless in agricultural administration, and his governance produced results of exceptional merit; Fiscal Commissioner Bao Zheng and the circuit envoys jointly reported his achievements, and when Emperor Renzong heard of them he issued an edict of praise, promoted Shangkuan in rank, and bestowed gold.

sentences.zh: 留於唐凡五年，民像以祠，而王安石、蘇軾作《新田》、《新渠》詩以美之。

translations.literal: He remained at Tang for five years in all; the people set up his image in a shrine, and Wang Anshi and Su Shi wrote poems "New Fields" and "New Channels" to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at Tangzhou for five years in all; the people erected his image in a shrine, and Wang Anshi and Su Shi wrote the poems "New Fields" and "New Channels" in praise of him.

sentences.zh: 徙同、宿二州，河中府神勇卒苦大校貪虐，刊匿名書告變，尚寬命焚之，曰：「妄言耳。」

translations.literal: Transferred to the two prefectures Tong and Su; at Hedong Prefecture the Shenyong garrison soldiers suffered under their commander's greed and cruelty; they posted an anonymous letter reporting a mutiny; Shangkuan ordered it burned, saying: "Idle talk."
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Tong and Su prefectures, he learned that at Hedong Prefecture the Shenyong garrison troops were suffering under their commander's greed and cruelty; they posted an anonymous letter reporting a mutiny, but Shangkuan ordered it burned, saying, "This is empty rumor."

sentences.zh: 眾乃安。

translations.literal: The crowd then settled down.
translations.idiomatic: The troops then calmed down.

sentences.zh: 已而奏黜校，分士卒隸他營。

translations.literal: Later he memorialized to dismiss the commander and divide the troops among other camps.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to dismiss the commander and divide the troops among other camps.

sentences.zh: 又徙梓州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again, this time to Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 尚寬去唐數歲，田日加辟，戶日益眾，朝廷推功，自少府監以直龍圖閣知梓州。

translations.literal: Several years after Shangkuan left Tang, fields were daily further opened and households daily grew more numerous; the court credited the achievement, and from Director of the Imperial Manufactories he was made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years after Shangkuan left Tangzhou, its fields were being opened day by day and its population was steadily growing; the court credited his earlier work, and he was promoted from director of the Imperial Manufactories to direct academician in the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 積官至司農卿，卒，詔賜錢五十萬。

translations.literal: Accumulating offices to Minister of Agriculture, he died; an edict bestowed five hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Minister of Agriculture, and when he died an edict bestowed five hundred thousand cash on his family.

sentences.zh: 高賦子正臣，中山人。

translations.literal: Gao Fu, styled Zhengchen, was a man of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Fu, courtesy name Zhengchen, was a native of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 以父任為右班殿直。

translations.literal: Through his father's yin privilege he became a Right Guard Duty Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's yin privilege he entered service as a Right Guard Duty Attendant.

sentences.zh: 復舉進士，改奉禮郎，四遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He also passed the jinshi examination, was changed to Gentleman for Ceremonial Purposes, and was promoted four times to Doctor of the Imperial Sacrificial Office.
translations.idiomatic: He also passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Gentleman for Ceremonial Purposes, and was promoted four times to doctor in the Imperial Sacrificial Office.

sentences.zh: 歷知真定縣，通判劍邢石州、成德軍。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Zhending County and as vice prefect of Jian, Xing, and Shi prefectures and Chengdé Military Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Zhending County and as vice prefect of Jian, Xing, and Shi prefectures and of Chengdé Military Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知衢州，俗尚巫鬼，民毛氏、柴氏二十餘家世蓄蠱毒，值閏歲，害人尤多，與人忿爭輒毒之。

translations.literal: As prefect of Quzhou, where custom honored witchcraft and ghosts, more than twenty households of the Mao and Chai clans for generations kept poisonous gu; in intercalary years they harmed people especially often, and whenever they quarreled with others they would poison them.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Quzhou, where the people honored witchcraft and spirits, more than twenty households of the Mao and Chai clans had for generations kept poisonous gu; in intercalary years they harmed people especially often, and whenever they quarreled with someone they would poison that person.

sentences.zh: 賦悉擒治伏辜，蠱患遂絕。

translations.literal: Fu captured and punished them all according to law; the gu scourge was then ended.
translations.idiomatic: Fu captured them all, punished them according to law, and the gu scourge was ended.

sentences.zh: 徙唐州，州田經百年曠不耕，前守趙尚寬菑墾不遺力，而榛莽者尚多。

translations.literal: Transferred to Tangzhou; the prefecture's fields had lain fallow untended for a century; the former prefect Zhao Shangkuan had opened wasteland without sparing effort, yet much scrubland still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Tangzhou, he found that its fields had lain fallow for a century; the former prefect Zhao Shangkuan had opened wasteland with tireless effort, yet much land was still overgrown.

sentences.zh: 賦繼其後，益募兩河流民，計口給田使耕，作陂堰四十四。

translations.literal: Fu followed after him, further recruiting migrants from the two Yellow River regions, allotting fields by head count for cultivation, and building forty-four reservoirs and dams.
translations.idiomatic: Fu followed in his footsteps, further recruiting migrants from the regions along the two Yellow Rivers, allotting fields by head count for cultivation, and building forty-four reservoirs and dams.

sentences.zh: 再滿再留，比其去，田增辟三萬一千三百餘頃，戶增萬一千三百八十，歲益稅二萬二千二百五十七。

translations.literal: He served two full terms and was kept on twice; by the time he left, newly opened fields increased by 31,300-plus qing, households by 11,380, and annual tax revenue by 22,257.
translations.idiomatic: He completed two full terms and was kept on twice; by the time he left, newly opened fields had increased by more than 31,300 qing, households by 11,380, and annual tax revenue by 22,257.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒諭，宣布治狀以勸天下，兩州為生立祠。

translations.literal: An imperial letter praised and commended him, proclaiming his record of governance to encourage the empire; both prefectures erected living shrines to him.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter praised and commended him, proclaiming his record of governance to encourage officials throughout the empire, and both prefectures erected living shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 擢提點河東刑獄，又加直龍圖閣、知滄州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Judicial Intendant of Hedong, then additionally made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judicial intendant of Hedong, then additionally made direct academician in the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and prefect of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 程昉欲於境內開西流河，繞州城而北註三塘泊。

translations.literal: Cheng Fang wished to open the Xiliu River within the jurisdiction, circling the prefectural city northward to pour into Santang Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Fang wanted to open the Xiliu River within the prefecture, routing it around the city to the north and into Santang Marsh.

sentences.zh: 賦曰：「滄城近河，歲增堤防，猶懼奔溢，矧妄有開鑿乎？」

translations.literal: Fu said: "Cangzhou city is close to the river; each year we add to the dikes, yet still fear a breach — how much more reckless to dig open channels at will?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "Cangzhou city lies close to the river; every year we raise the dikes, yet still fear a breach — how much more reckless would it be to dig open new channels?"

sentences.zh: 昉執不從，後功竟不成。

translations.literal: Fang stubbornly would not listen; afterward the work ultimately was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Fang stubbornly refused to listen, and in the end the project was never completed.

sentences.zh: 歷蔡、潞二州，入同判太常寺，進集賢院學士。

translations.literal: He served the two prefectures Cai and Lu, entered as associate judge of the Imperial Sacrificial Office, and advanced to academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Cai and Lu prefectures, entered the capital as associate judge of the Imperial Sacrificial Office, and was promoted to academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 在朝多所建明，嘗言：「二府大臣或僦舍委巷，散處京城，公私非便。

translations.literal: In court he proposed many things; once he said: "Grand councilors of the two administrations sometimes rent lodgings in back alleys, scattered throughout the capital — inconvenient for public and private affairs alike.
translations.idiomatic: While at court he proposed many reforms; once he said, "Grand councilors of the two administrations sometimes rent lodgings in back alleys, scattered across the capital — this is inconvenient for both public business and private life.

sentences.zh: 宜仿前代丞相府，於端門前列置大第，俾居之。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow prior dynasties' model of a chief minister's mansion, setting up great residences in rows before the Gate of Correct Demeanor, and having them dwell there."
translations.idiomatic: We should follow the model of earlier dynasties' chief-minister mansions and set up great residences in rows before the Gate of Correct Demeanor for them to live in."

sentences.zh: 又言：「仁宗朝為兗國公主治第，用錢數十萬緡。

translations.literal: He also said: "In Renzong's reign a residence was built for Princess Yan'guo, costing several hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In Emperor Renzong's reign a residence was built for Princess Yan'guo at a cost of several hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 今有五大長公主，若悉如前比，其費無藝。

translations.literal: Now there are five great senior princesses; if all are treated by the previous standard, the expense would be boundless.
translations.idiomatic: There are now five great senior princesses; if all were treated on that scale, the expense would know no limit.

sentences.zh: 願講求中制，裁為定式。」

translations.literal: I wish to seek a moderate standard and cut it to a fixed regulation."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a moderate standard be worked out and fixed as a permanent rule."

sentences.zh: 請諸道提點刑獄司置檢法官，庶專平讞，使民不冤。

translations.literal: He requested that judicial intendant offices on all circuits appoint reviewing judges, so that reviews of cases might be specialized and equitable, and the people not suffer injustice.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that judicial intendant offices on all circuits appoint reviewing judges, so that case review would be specialized and fair and the people would not suffer injustice.

sentences.zh: 乞於禁中建閣，繪功臣像，如漢雲臺、唐淩煙之制。

translations.literal: He petitioned to build a hall within the palace precinct and paint portraits of meritorious ministers, on the model of Han's Cloud Terrace and Tang's Lingyan.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to build a hall within the palace precinct and paint portraits of meritorious ministers, following the models of the Han Cloud Terrace and the Tang Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 言多施行。

translations.literal: Many of his proposals were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his proposals were adopted and carried out.

sentences.zh: 以通議大夫致仕，退居襄陽，卒年八十四。

translations.literal: He retired as Master of Court Counsel and lived in retirement at Xiangyang; he died at age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the rank of Master of Court Counsel and withdrew to Xiangyang, where he died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 程師孟，字公辟，吳人。

translations.literal: Cheng Shimeng, styled Gongbi, was a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Shimeng, courtesy name Gongbi, was a native of Wu.

sentences.zh: 進士甲科。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the first grade.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 累知南康軍、楚州，提點夔路刑獄。

translations.literal: He successively governed Nankang Military Prefecture and Chuzhou, and served as judicial intendant of the Kuí circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He successively governed Nankang Military Prefecture and Chuzhou and served as judicial intendant of the Kuí circuit.

sentences.zh: 瀘戎數犯渝州邊，使者治所在萬州，相去遠，有警，率浹日乃至。

translations.literal: The Lu barbarians repeatedly violated the border of Yuzhou; the envoy's administrative seat was at Wanzhou, far away — when there was an alarm, it usually took about ten days to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu tribes repeatedly raided the border of Yuzhou, but the judicial envoy's seat was at Wanzhou, far away; when an alarm arose, it usually took about ten days for help to arrive.

sentences.zh: 師孟奏徙於渝。

translations.literal: Shimeng memorialized to move it to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng memorialized to move the envoy's seat to Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 夔部無常平粟，建請置倉，適凶歲，振民不足，即矯發他儲，不俟報。

translations.literal: In the Kuí region there was no ever-normal grain; he proposed establishing granaries; when a famine year came and relief grain was insufficient, he immediately issued grain from other stores on his own authority, without awaiting approval.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuí region had no ever-normal granary grain, so he proposed establishing granaries; when a famine year came and relief grain ran short, he immediately issued grain from other stores on his own authority without waiting for approval.

sentences.zh: 吏懼，白不可，師孟曰：「必俟報，俄者盡死矣。」

translations.literal: Officials were afraid and reported it could not be done; Shimeng said: "If we must await approval, soon they will all be dead."
translations.idiomatic: The officials were alarmed and reported that this could not be done, but Shimeng said, "If we wait for approval, they will all be dead before it comes."

sentences.zh: 竟發之。

translations.literal: In the end he issued it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he issued the grain anyway.

sentences.zh: 徙河東路。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Hedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 晉地多土山，旁接川谷，春夏大雨，水濁如黃河，俗謂之「天河」，可溉灌。

translations.literal: Jin territory has many earthen hills connecting to valleys; in spring and summer heavy rains make the water muddy like the Yellow River; custom calls it the "Heaven River," and it can be used for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin region has many earthen hills linked to valleys; in spring and summer heavy rains turn the water muddy like the Yellow River, and local custom calls it the "Heaven River"; it can be used for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 師孟勸民出錢開渠築堰，淤良田萬八千頃，裒其事為《水利圖經》，頒之州縣。

translations.literal: Shimeng urged the people to contribute money to open channels and build dams, enriching eighteen thousand qing of fine farmland; he gathered the matter into "Illustrated Record of Waterworks" and distributed it to prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng urged the people to contribute money to open channels and build dams, bringing eighteen thousand qing of fine farmland under cultivation; he compiled an account of the project as the "Illustrated Record of Waterworks" and distributed it to prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 為度支判官。

translations.literal: He served as fiscal review commissioner in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as fiscal review commissioner in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 知洪州，積石為江堤，浚章溝，揭北閘，以節水升降，後無水患。

translations.literal: As prefect of Hongzhou, he piled stone for a river dike, dredged the Zhang Channel, raised the north sluice gate to regulate the water's rise and fall; afterward there were no flood disasters.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Hongzhou, he piled stone to build a river dike, dredged the Zhang Channel, and raised the north sluice gate to regulate the water's rise and fall; afterward the region suffered no more flood disasters.

sentences.zh: 判三司都磨勘司，接拌契丹使，蕭惟輔曰：「白溝之地當兩屬，今南朝植柳數里，而以北人漁界河為罪，豈理也哉？」

translations.literal: As judge of the Three Offices' Central Audit Bureau, he received the Khitan envoys; Xiao Weifu said: "The lands of the Bai Gou should belong to both sides; now the Southern Court has planted willows for miles, yet treats northerners fishing on the border river as a crime — is that reasonable?"
translations.idiomatic: As judge of the Three Offices' Central Audit Bureau, he received the Khitan envoys; Xiao Weifu said, "The lands along the Bai Gou should belong to both sides; now the Southern Court has planted willows for miles, yet treats northerners fishing on the border river as a crime — is that reasonable?"

sentences.zh: 師孟曰：「兩朝當守誓約，涿郡有案牘可覆視，君舍文書，騰口說，詎欲生事耶？」

translations.literal: Shimeng said: "Both courts should keep the sworn treaties; Zhuo Prefecture has documents that can be reviewed; you discard written records and flap your mouth — do you wish to stir up trouble?"
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng said, "Both courts should keep the sworn treaties; Zhuo Prefecture has documents that can be reviewed. You discard the written records and wag your tongue — do you mean to stir up trouble?"

sentences.zh: 惟輔愧謝。

translations.literal: Weifu apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Weifu apologized in embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 出為江西轉運使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as transport commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as transport commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 盜發袁州，州吏為耳目，久不獲，師孟械吏數輩送獄，盜即成擒。

translations.literal: Robbers struck in Yuanzhou; prefectural clerks served as their eyes and ears; for a long time they were not caught; Shimeng shackled several clerks and sent them to prison, and the robbers were immediately captured.
translations.idiomatic: When robbers struck in Yuanzhou, prefectural clerks served as their eyes and ears, and for a long time the culprits could not be caught; Shimeng shackled several clerks and sent them to prison, and the robbers were captured at once.

sentences.zh: 加直昭文館，知福州，築子城，建學舍，治行最東南。

translations.literal: He was given direct appointment in the Hall of Brilliant Literature and made prefect of Fuzhou; he built an inner city wall and established school buildings; his record of governance ranked first in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Given direct appointment in the Hall of Brilliant Literature, he served as prefect of Fuzhou, built an inner city wall, and established school buildings; his record of governance ranked first in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 徙廣州，州城為儂寇所毀，他日有警，民駭竄，方伯相踵至，皆言土疏惡不可築。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guangzhou; the prefectural wall had been destroyed by Nong bandits; on another day when there was an alarm the people fled in panic; successive governors all said the soil was loose and poor and could not be built upon.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guangzhou, he found the prefectural wall had been destroyed by Nong bandits; when another alarm came the people fled in panic, and successive governors had all said the soil was loose and poor and could not support construction.

sentences.zh: 師孟在廣六年，作西城，及交址陷邕管，聞廣守備固，不敢東。

translations.literal: Shimeng was at Guang six years, building the western wall; when Jiaozhi took Yong and Guan, hearing Guangzhou's defenses were solid, they did not dare move east.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng spent six years at Guangzhou building the western wall; when Jiaozhi took Yong and Guan, the enemy heard that Guangzhou's defenses were strong and did not dare advance eastward.

sentences.zh: 時師孟已召還，朝廷念前功，以為給事中、集賢殿修撰，判都水監。

translations.literal: By then Shimeng had already been recalled; the court mindful of his prior service made him Supervising Secretary, compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and concurrent director of the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shimeng had already been recalled to the capital; mindful of his earlier service, the court appointed him Supervising Secretary, compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and concurrent director of the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 賀契丹主生辰，至涿州，契丹命席，迎者正南向，涿州官西向，宋使價東向。

translations.literal: To congratulate the Khitan ruler's birthday, arriving at Zhuo Prefecture, the Khitan arranged the seating — those receiving faced due south, Zhuo officials west, and Song envoys east.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to congratulate the Khitan ruler on his birthday, he arrived at Zhuo Prefecture, where the Khitan arranged the seating with those receiving the envoys facing due south, Zhuo officials facing west, and the Song envoys facing east.

sentences.zh: 師孟曰：「是卑我也。」

translations.literal: Shimeng said: "This is to demean me."
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng said, "This is meant to demean me."

sentences.zh: 不就列，自日昃爭至暮，從者失色，師孟辭氣益厲，叱儐者易之，於是更與迎者東西向。

translations.literal: He would not take his place; from mid-afternoon they argued until evening; his attendants turned pale; Shimeng's tone grew ever sharper; he shouted at the ushers to change it; thereupon he and those receiving faced each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to take his seat and argued from mid-afternoon until evening; his attendants turned pale, but Shimeng's tone grew ever sharper; he shouted at the ushers to change the arrangement, and at last he and those receiving the envoys faced each other east and west.

sentences.zh: 明日，涿人錢於郊，疾馳過不顧，涿人移雄州以為言，坐罷歸班。

translations.literal: Next day the people of Zhuo offered money in the suburbs; he galloped past without a glance; the Zhuo people reported to Xiongzhou; for this he was dismissed and returned to the regular ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the people of Zhuo offered money in the suburbs; he galloped past without stopping to acknowledge them; the Zhuo people complained to Xiongzhou, and for this he was dismissed and returned to the regular ranks.

sentences.zh: 復起知越州、青州，遂致仕，以光祿大夫卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He was again raised to serve as prefect of Yuezhou and Qingzhou, then retired; he died as Grandee for Splendid Happiness at age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed prefect of Yuezhou and Qingzhou, then retired; he died with the rank of Grandee for Splendid Happiness at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 師孟累領劇鎮，為政簡而嚴，罪非死者不以屬吏。

translations.literal: Shimeng repeatedly held important prefectures; his governance was simple yet stern; crimes not punishable by death he did not turn over to subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng repeatedly held important prefectures; his governance was simple yet stern, and he never delegated to subordinates cases that did not carry the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 發隱擿伏如神，得豪惡不逞跌宕者必痛懲艾之，至剿絕乃已，所部肅然。

translations.literal: Uncovering hidden wrongs he was like a spirit; when he got violent, overbearing scoundrels he always punished severely, not stopping until they were rooted out; his jurisdictions were orderly and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: He uncovered hidden wrongs with uncanny skill; whenever he caught violent, overbearing scoundrels he punished them severely and did not stop until they were rooted out, and his jurisdictions were orderly and quiet.

sentences.zh: 洪、福、廣、越為立生祠。

translations.literal: Hong, Fu, Guang, and Yue erected living shrines to him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures of Hong, Fu, Guang, and Yue erected living shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 韓晉卿，字伯修，密州安丘人。

translations.literal: Han Jinqing, styled Boxiu, was a native of Anqiu in Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jinqing, courtesy name Boxiu, came from Anqiu in Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 為童子時，日誦書數千言。

translations.literal: As a boy, he daily recited several thousand characters from the books.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he recited several thousand characters of text each day.

sentences.zh: 長以《五經》中第，歷肥鄉嘉興主簿、安肅軍司法參軍、平城令大理詳斷、審刑詳議官，通判應天府，知同州、壽州，奏課第一，擢刑部郎中。

translations.literal: When grown he passed the Five Classics examination, and successively served as Registrar of Feixiang and Jiaxing, Judicial Military Adjutant of Ansujun, Magistrate of Pingcheng, Detailed Adjudicator of the Court of Judicial Review, Detailed Deliberation Official of the Office of Scrutiny for Punishments, Administrative Assistant of Yingtian Prefecture, and Prefect of Tongzhou and Shouzhou; ranked first in memorialized evaluations and was promoted to Supervisor in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he passed the Five Classics examination and rose through posts as registrar in Feixiang and Jiaxing, judicial adjutant at Ansujun, magistrate of Pingcheng, detailed adjudicator at the Court of Judicial Review, and deliberation officer at the Office of Scrutiny for Punishments, then served as administrative assistant at Yingtian Prefecture and prefect of Tongzhou and Shouzhou; when his performance reports ranked first, he was promoted to supervisor in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，知明州，兩浙轉運使差役法復行，諸道處畫多倉卒失敘，獨晉卿視民所宜而不戾法指。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou reign, as Prefect of Mingzhou, when the Two Zhe Transport Commissioner reimplemented the Corvée Service Law, the various circuits mostly worked out plans in haste without proper order; only Jinqing considered what suited the people without violating the intent of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era, as prefect of Mingzhou, he faced the reintroduction of the corvée service law by the Two Zhe transport commissioner; most circuits rushed out plans in disorder, but Jinqing alone tailored arrangements to the people's needs without straying from the law's purpose.

sentences.zh: 入為大理少卿，遷卿。

translations.literal: He entered [court] as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review and was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and later promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 晉卿自仁宗朝已典訟臬，時朝廷有疑議，輒下公卿雜議。

translations.literal: Jinqing had managed judicial affairs since the Renzong reign; whenever the court had doubtful disputes, they would refer them for joint deliberation among ministers and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing had overseen legal cases since Emperor Renzong's reign; whenever the court faced a doubtful dispute, the case was sent down for joint deliberation among the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 開封民爭鶉殺人，王安石以為盜拒捕鬥而死，殺之無罪，晉卿曰：「是鬥殺也。」

translations.literal: In Kaifeng a commoner killed someone in a fight over quail; Wang Anshi held that the victim died resisting arrest as a thief and that killing him was not a crime. Jinqing said: "This is brawling with fatal result."
translations.idiomatic: In Kaifeng a man killed another in a quarrel over quail; Wang Anshi argued the victim had died resisting arrest as a thief and that the killer was innocent. Jinqing said, "This is brawling homicide."

sentences.zh: 登州婦人謀殺夫，郡守許遵執為按問，安石復主之，晉卿曰：「當死。」

translations.literal: In Dengzhou a woman plotted to murder her husband; the prefect Xu Zun insisted it was interrogation under torture; Anshi again supported him. Jinqing said: "She should die."
translations.idiomatic: In Dengzhou a woman plotted her husband's murder; Prefect Xu Zun treated it as a case of interrogation under torture, and Anshi again backed him. Jinqing said, "She deserves death."

sentences.zh: 事久不決，爭論盈庭，終持之不肯變，用是知名。

translations.literal: The matter long went unresolved; debate filled the court; in the end he held to his view and would not change—through this he became famous.
translations.idiomatic: The case dragged on unresolved while debate filled the court, but he held firm and would not yield—and through this he won renown.

sentences.zh: 元豐置大理獄，多內庭所付，晉卿持平考核，無所上下。

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng the Court of Judicial Review prison was reestablished; many cases were assigned from the inner palace. Jinqing weighed them impartially and showed favoritism to none.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanfeng era the Court of Judicial Review prison was restored, and many cases came down from the inner palace; Jinqing reviewed them evenhandedly, favoring no one.

sentences.zh: 神宗稱其才，每讞獄雖明，若事連貴要、屢鞠弗成者，必以委之，嘗被詔按治寧州獄，循故事當入對，晉卿曰：「奉使有指，三尺法具在，豈應刺候主意，輕重其心乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong praised his talent. Though reviews were usually clear, whenever a case involved powerful persons and repeated interrogations failed, it was always entrusted to him. Once ordered to investigate the Ningzhou prison, according to precedent he should have entered court for audience. Jinqing said: "The imperial commission has its charge; the full body of law is there—how should one probe the sovereign's intentions and weigh gains in one's mind?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong praised his ability; though most case reviews were straightforward, any matter touching powerful figures that resisted repeated interrogation was always put in his hands. Once, ordered to investigate the Ningzhou prison, he was expected by precedent to enter court for an audience. Jinqing said, "The commission has its charge and the law is complete—why should I probe the emperor's mind and weigh my own advantage?"

sentences.zh: 受命即行。

translations.literal: Having received the order, he departed at once.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted the order and set out immediately.

sentences.zh: 諸州請讞大辟，執政惡其多，將劾不應讞者。

translations.literal: When prefectures petitioned to review capital sentences, the chief ministers disliked the volume and were about to impeach those who did not seek review.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectures petitioned for review of capital sentences, the chief ministers resented the volume and were ready to impeach officials who failed to seek review.

sentences.zh: 晉卿曰：「聽斷求所以生之，仁恩之至也。

translations.literal: Jinqing said: "In hearing cases and passing judgment, to seek grounds by which to let live is the utmost of benevolence and grace.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing said, "In judging cases, to seek every ground for sparing life is the height of humane governance.

sentences.zh: 茍讞而獲譴，後不來矣。」

translations.literal: If review brings reprimand, later [officials] will not come forward."
translations.idiomatic: If seeking review brings punishment, officials will stop coming forward."

sentences.zh: 議者又欲引唐日覆奏，令天下庶戮悉奏決。

translations.literal: The debaters also wanted to cite the Tang practice of daily re-submission, requiring all ordinary executions throughout the realm to be memorialized for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Others proposed reviving the Tang practice of daily re-submission, so that every ordinary execution in the empire would require a memorial decision from court.

sentences.zh: 晉卿言：「可疑可矜者許上請，祖宗之制也。

translations.literal: Jinqing said: "Allowing appeal where there is doubt or grounds for mercy—the institutions of the ancestral emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing argued, "Permitting appeal in doubtful or pitiable cases was the institution of the founding emperors.

sentences.zh: 四海萬里，必須系以聽朝命，恐自今庾死者多於伏辜者矣。」

translations.literal: Across ten thousand li of the four seas, all must be held awaiting the court's command—I fear that from now on those dying in prison will outnumber those who pay for their crimes."
translations.idiomatic: Across the realm's ten thousand li, every prisoner would have to wait on the court's word—I fear more would die in custody than ever pay for their crimes."

sentences.zh: 朝廷皆行其說，故士大夫間推其忠厚，不以法家名之。

translations.literal: The court adopted all his proposals; hence among scholar-officials he was praised for his generosity and was not styled a Legalist.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposals, and among scholar-officials he was admired for his humane breadth rather than branded a Legalist.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 葉康直，字景溫，建州人。

translations.literal: Ye Kangzhi, styled Jingwen, was from Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Kangzhi, courtesy name Jingwen, was a native of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，知光化縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became Magistrate of Guanghua County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Guanghua County.

sentences.zh: 縣多竹，民皆編為屋，康直教用陶瓦，以寧火患。

translations.literal: The county had much bamboo; the people wove it into houses. Kangzhi taught them to use ceramic tiles to ease the risk of fire.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo was abundant in the county and people wove it into their houses; Kangzhi taught them to use ceramic tiles instead, reducing the danger of fire.

sentences.zh: 凡政皆務以利民。

translations.literal: In all governance he strove to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: In every policy he sought the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 時豐稷為谷城令，亦以治績顯，人歌之曰：「葉光化，豐谷城，清如水，平如衡。」

translations.literal: At the time Feng Ji was Magistrate of Gucheng and also distinguished himself by administrative achievements; people sang of them: "Ye of Guanghua, Feng of Gucheng—clear as water, level as a balance."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ji was then magistrate of Gucheng and likewise won renown for his governance; people sang of them, "Ye of Guanghua, Feng of Gucheng—clear as water, even as a balance scale."

sentences.zh: 曾布行新法，以為司農屬。

translations.literal: When Zeng Bu implemented the New Policies, [Kangzhi] was made an official of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Bu carried out the New Policies, Kangzhi was appointed to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 歷永興、秦鳳轉運判官，徙陜西，進提點刑獄、轉運副使。

translations.literal: He served successively as Transport Commissioner of Yongxing and Qinfeng, transferred to Shaanxi, and advanced to Judicial Intendant and Vice Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as transport commissioner for Yongxing and Qinfeng, transferred to Shaanxi, and rose to judicial intendant and vice transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五路兵西征，康直領涇原糧道，承受內侍梁同以餉惡妄奏，神宗怒，械康直，將誅之，王安禮力救，得歸故官。

translations.literal: When armies of the five circuits marched west, Kangzhi oversaw the grain route in Jingyuan; the palace attendant Liang Tong, charged with receiving supplies, falsely memorialized that the provisions were bad; Shenzong was angry, had Kangzhi shackled, and was about to execute him; Wang Anli vigorously interceded and he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: During the western campaign of the five-circuit armies, Kangzhi managed the grain route in Jingyuan; the palace attendant Liang Tong, responsible for receiving supplies, falsely reported that the rations were spoiled; Emperor Shenzong was enraged, had Kangzhi shackled, and was about to execute him; Wang Anli interceded forcefully, and he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，加直龍圖閣，知秦州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was given direct appointment to the Longtu Pavilion and became Prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era he received direct appointment to the Longtu Pavilion and became prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人曾肇、蘇轍劾康直諂事李憲，免官，究實無狀，改知河中府，復為秦州。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Secretariat Zeng Zhao and Su Che impeached Kangzhi for fawning on Li Xian; he was dismissed, but investigation found no substance; he was reassigned as Prefect of Hezhong Prefecture and later returned to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Zeng Zhao and Su Che impeached Kangzhi for currying favor with Li Xian; he was dismissed, but investigation found no basis for the charge; he was reassigned prefect of Hezhong and later returned to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏人侵甘谷，康直戒諸將設伏以待，殲其二酋，自是不敢犯境。

translations.literal: When the Xi Xia invaded Gangu, Kangzhi instructed the generals to lay ambush; two of their chieftains were destroyed, and thereafter they did not dare violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut Xi Xia raided Gangu, Kangzhi ordered the generals to set an ambush; two enemy chieftains were killed, and from then on they did not dare cross the border.

sentences.zh: 進寶文閣待制、陜西都運使。

translations.literal: He advanced to Secretariat Drafter of the Baowen Pavilion and Grand Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafter of the Baowen Pavilion and grand transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 以疾請知亳州，通浚積潦，民獲田數十萬畝。

translations.literal: Illness led him to request assignment as Prefect of Bozhou; he dredged accumulated floodwaters, and the people gained several hundred thousand mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: On grounds of illness he requested appointment as prefect of Bozhou; he dredged stagnant floodwaters, and the people recovered several hundred thousand mu of farmland.

sentences.zh: 召為兵部侍郎，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: Summoned as Vice Minister of War, he died at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice minister of war but died at sixty-four.
